# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light from #4481

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`review/step3-routing.md` gives each Step 3 Routing log line as a template (`STAGED {time} — Step 3 Routing: {severity}-severity finding {category} at {file:line}. Stage path: …`) that the caller fills by hand and passes to `plugin/bin/log-decision.js` as `--text`, with `--step "Step 3 Routing"`. `log-decision.js` already writes `{step}: ` before the text, so a caller who copies the template's `Step 3 Routing:` into `--text` gets `Step 3 Routing: Step 3 Routing: …` — nothing checks for it. The severity token is also hand-ordered: #4481's review logged `high-severity security finding at …` instead of `high-severity finding security at …`, and `/claude-tweaks:release` Step 3 classifies its gate by the literal token `high-severity finding`, so that line would have read as no blocking finding. Observed in run 2026-10-27T184830-spec-4481: 13 lines carried the doubled prefix and 3 STAGED lines the mis-ordered token; they were rewritten in place by hand. Probes: `git log -S "startsWith(o.step" --oneline origin/main -- plugin/bin/log-decision.js plugin/bin/lib` and `git grep -n -i -e "repeats --step" -e "step prefix" -e "duplicated step" origin/main -- plugin/bin` both returned nothing, and no open issue matched `log-decision step prefix`.

## Deliverables

`log-decision.js` refuses (exit 2, naming both values) a `--text` or `--entries` text that begins with its own `--step` value followed by `:`.

A composer for review routing lines, `--severity`, `--category` and `--at` flags or a small `review-routing-line.js`, so `{severity}-severity finding {category} at {file:line}` is never hand-typed; `step3-routing.md` cites it in place of the free-text template.

A test that feeds the composed STAGED and KEPT-PROMPT lines through the same token match `/claude-tweaks:release` Step 3 applies and sees `review: blocking`.

## Acceptance Criteria

`node plugin/bin/log-decision.js --run <dir> --status AUTO --step "Step 3 Routing" --text "Step 3 Routing: x"` exits 2 and writes nothing.

A high finding routed through the composer produces a line containing the literal `high-severity finding`.

Each new test fails with its change reverted.

## Release Note

Review routing log lines are composed by a CLI, so the release gate always sees a staged high or critical finding.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/log-decision.js` — refuse a --text that repeats --step
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — cite the routing-line composer

Origin: SDD ruling ratified at Review Console (#4481, staged/sdd-ruling-2.md)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` walks a function definition's body (`g() { … }`, `function g { … }`) once, as a group where it is defined, so a `cd` in it reaches the commands after the definition. A later call from another cwd is not re-walked: `f() { echo z > k; }; cd ../wt; f` writes `wt/k` in bash 3.2, bash 5 and zsh, while base and every #4481 revision report `r/k`. Not case-specific. #4481's SDD Task 1 ruled it deferred to its own record at Important (ledger row 15); `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` lists it as a known gap ("a function body when the function is called later from another cwd").

## Deliverables

Record each function name defined in a walked command with its body text, and when a later segment's command word is that name, walk the body under that segment's cwds (bounded, so a recursive or re-defined function cannot loop).

Pin `f() { echo z > k; }; cd ../wt; f` (wt/k) and a redefinition case, with bash 3.2/5 verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

`fileWriteTargets('f() { echo z > k; }; cd ../wt; f', '/r/x')` includes `/r/wt/k`.

Each new test fails with the change reverted; the hook suites pass; the known-gaps clause is removed from policy-schema-coverage.md.

## Release Note

The worktree write gate follows a write inside a shell function to the cwd the function is called from.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — re-walk a function body at its call site
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — pin the call-site shapes
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` — drop the known-gap clause

Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s cd walk assumes a `case` arm always runs, so a `cd` in an arm reaches the commands after `esac` even when no pattern matches. `case $x in a) cd /wt;; esac; echo x > f` resolves only `/wt/f`; bash 3.2 and 5 write `./f` when `$x` is not `a`. Pre-existing; #4481 (ledger row 1, SDD Task 1 review) recorded it, and `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` lists it as a known gap ("a case arm whose pattern does not match").

## Deliverables

After a `case` whose arms carry no catch-all `*)` pattern, carry the cwd before the case as well as each arm's cwd into the commands after `esac`, failing closed.

Pin `case $x in a) cd /wt;; esac; echo x > f` (both `/wt/f` and `./f`) and the catch-all form `case $x in a) cd /wt;; *) cd /q;; esac; echo x > f` (no `./f`), with bash 3.2/5 verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

`fileWriteTargets('case $x in a) cd /wt;; esac; echo x > f', '/r')` includes `/r/f` and `/wt/f`.

Each new test fails with the change reverted; the hook suites pass; the known-gaps clause is removed from policy-schema-coverage.md.

## Release Note

The worktree write gate no longer assumes a `case` arm runs when no pattern may match.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — join the pre-case cwd after a case with no catch-all
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — pin both shapes
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` — drop the known-gap clause

Origin: /claude-tweaks:release v6.156.3 Step 8 disposition (run 2026-10-27T161535-release-standalone)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

A confirmed review finding that has no code fix (a record proposal) has no staging name that both ends of the pipeline accept:

- `review/step3-routing.md` only ever stages `staged/review-{n}.patch` (line 58). It names no `.md` shape for a confirmed finding that becomes a record.
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` SECTION_MAP matches `review-{n}` only through its `/\.patch$/` row, so `stage-item.js --id review-3` for a `.md` is refused `unmapped-prefix`. The nearest canonical prefix it suggests is `review-followup-` (QUEUE section), which no skill produces.
- `plugin/skills/release/disposition.md`'s Review staging roster lists `review-{n}` as `staged/review-{n}.{md,patch}` (route `confirmed`) and has no `review-followup-` row, so the one name stage-item accepts is off the disposition roster.

Hit in run `2026-10-27T161535-release-standalone` (v6.156.3): five record proposals were staged as `review-followup-1..5.md` and Step 8 disposition had to read and settle them by hand (logged as a note in that run's decisions.md).

## Deliverables

1. `review/step3-routing.md` names the staging shape for a confirmed finding routed to a record (no patch): `staged/review-followup-{n}.md`, written via `stage-item.js`, carrying the `Title:`/`Type:`/`Labels:`/`Defer-reason:` header the console's queue-write step reads.
2. `release/disposition.md`'s Review staging roster gains a `review-followup-` row (route `proposal`, counted one finding per file), and the `review-{n}` row's example narrows to `staged/review-{n}.patch` — the `.md` alternative is removed because nothing can stage it.
3. A test pins that every prefix in disposition.md's roster with a non-`not staged by review` route is either accepted by `stage-item.js` (classifies mapped) or matches the `.patch` row, so the roster and SECTION_MAP cannot drift apart again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node plugin/bin/stage-item.js --run <dir> --id review-followup-1 …` with a `.md` body succeeds, and release Step 8 disposition routes the file through its Routing table without a hand-disposal note.
- [ ] disposition.md's roster has no row whose example a producer cannot stage (no `review-{n}.md`).
- [ ] The new roster-vs-SECTION_MAP test fails when the `review-followup-` row is deleted from disposition.md, and passes with it.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — name the review-followup-{n}.md staging shape for a confirmed record-routed finding
- `plugin/skills/release/disposition.md` — add the review-followup- roster row; narrow review-{n} to .patch
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — read-only reference: SECTION_MAP / CANONICAL_PREFIXES the new test checks against

Origin: /claude-tweaks:release v6.156.2 release-gate review (run 2026-10-27T074620-release-standalone)

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

#4420 routed `checkResumeFreshness` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js`) and `parentLiveDetail` (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js`) through run-liveness via the shared `blocksResume`/`resumeEntries` helpers, but the extraction stopped halfway:

- **The resume ladder is hand-copied in both callers.** Lock positive → commit positive → `blocksResume` → `no-commits` → indeterminate, including the identical `(lock.result !== 'negative' ? lock : commit).detail` pick, at `resume-freshness.js:86-102` and `consolidated-pass.js:59-66`. `run-liveness/index.js`'s `blocksResume` comment says `no-commits` does not block because both callers handle it themselves, so the fail-closed `no-commits` rung lives in two copies kept in sync only by prose. No test asserts the two ladders agree: `tests/bin-lib/flow/consolidated-pass.test.js` stubs `checkResumeFreshness`.
- **`checkResumeFreshness` side-channels the commit time.** The `last-commit` evidence entry carries only `{result, detail}`, so `resume-freshness.js:83-85` wraps the probe in a closure that assigns an outer `commitAt` to compute `ageMs`. That only holds while `runLiveness` calls the injected probe exactly once and synchronously. If the default probe ran instead, `commitAt` would stay `null` and `ageMs` would silently read as `now`.

Found by the v6.156.2 release-gate whole-branch review (lens 3e, reproduced by both agents; cross-lens debate converged at medium; the consolidated-pass duplication separately tiebreak-confirmed). The release reviewed already-merged history, so it filed this rather than fixing it. `Premise-check:` exits 0 while the side channel is still present.

## Deliverables

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js`: one resume-verdict helper (e.g. `resumeVerdict(result)` → `{ kind: 'locked' | 'recent-commit' | 'indeterminate' | 'clear', entry, commitAgeMs }`) that owns the whole ladder, `no-commits` rung included. The `last-commit` evidence entry carries the commit time or age, so callers need no side channel.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js` and `plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js`: each maps that verdict to its own output shape (`{safe, verdict, reason, ageMs}` / detail string), keeping its own pre-probe status gates.
- One test that feeds the same evidence (lock error, commit error, `no-commits`, lock positive, commit positive, all negative) through both callers and asserts their verdict kinds agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git grep -n -F "commitAt = lastCommitAt" -- plugin/bin` prints nothing (it matches `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js:85` at 05dc74c).
- [ ] `git grep -n -F "(lock.result !== 'negative' ? lock : commit).detail" -- plugin/bin` prints nothing outside `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/` (it matches `consolidated-pass.js:63` and `resume-freshness.js:100` at 05dc74c).
- [ ] The agreement test above fails when the `no-commits` rung is removed from either caller's mapping and passes with both intact.
- [ ] Existing `tests/hooks-resume-freshness.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/flow/consolidated-pass.test.js` and `tests/run-liveness-callers-conformance.test.js` pass unchanged in behavior.

## Release Note

No user-visible change. Interrupted-run resume checks and the multi-spec consolidated-pass banner now share one fail-closed decision path.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js` — add the shared resume-verdict helper; carry commit age on the last-commit evidence entry
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js` — map the shared verdict; drop the commitAt closure
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js` — map the shared verdict instead of re-implementing the ladder
- `tests/run-liveness-callers-conformance.test.js` — or a new suite: assert both callers agree on the same evidence

_Filed by `release` via specShapedBody._

Origin: /claude-tweaks:tidy close-out 2026-10-27 (run 2026-10-27T055458-tidy-standalone)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

step-7-5-worktree-always.md says the arm step runs `gh pr merge --auto` and is "never an immediate merge (checks pending)". On a repository with no required checks GitHub merges at once: on 2026-10-27 housekeeping PR #4458 merged in the same second it was "armed", before any CI run on it. Its `test` workflow then ran only post-merge on main.

## Deliverables

Approach: Before arming, read whether the integration branch requires status checks. With none, `gh pr merge --auto` is an immediate merge, so wait for the PR's checks (bounded watch, as pr-first-merge Step 2.5 does) or leave it unarmed with the reason. Run the same closing-keyword screen build runs use on the composed housekeeping PR body before `gh pr create`.

1. Detect the no-required-checks case before arming and fall back to a bounded check watch, then merge or report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a repo without required checks, tidy never merges its housekeeping PR before the PR's own checks complete green.

## Release Note

Tidy's housekeeping PRs now wait for their checks and can no longer close an issue by accident.

**Related:** #4303, #4281, #4247

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build of #4303 (run 2026-10-25T143627-spec-4303), the origin/main catch-up merge (1b7caaca8)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Both shapes fail open at base d9aa6b82d, at main's #4281 and at the merged #4303 head 1b7caaca8. Checked with `fileWriteTargets` from cwd `/r`.

- `echo x > '(x'` resolves no target, but bash 3.2 and 5 write the file `/r/(x`. The redirect scan skips a target that starts with `(`, so that it never reads a process substitution as a file, and it does this even when the `(` is quoted.
- `cd>f /main; cp a g.js` resolves `/r/f` and `/r/g.js`. Bash writes `f` in `/r`, changes to `/main`, and writes `/main/g.js`. The cd walk reads the lead word `cd>f` as no `cd` at all, because the redirect is glued to the builtin name.

## Deliverables

1. Skip a redirect target as a process substitution only when its `(` is bare. A quoted or escaped `(` is file text.
2. Split a redirect glued to the lead word (`cd>f`, `cd>>f`) before reading the cd, so the cd and its redirect both apply.
3. Pin both shapes in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` with their bash 3.2 and 5 verdicts, per `.claude/skills/shell-scanner-bash-differential`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `echo x > '(x'` resolves `/r/(x`, and `cat <(true)` still resolves no target.
- `cd>f /main; cp a g.js` resolves `/r/f` and `/main/g.js`, so it is denied from a worktree whose main checkout is `/main`.
- Each rule has a red-turning mutant.
- The four scanner suites pass.

## Release Note

The worktree-always guard now catches a write to a quoted name starting with `(` and a `cd` written with a glued redirect.

**Related:** #4303

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build of #4303 (run 2026-10-25T143627-spec-4303), SDD final-review rounds 5-8

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

After the cwd cap is lost, `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js` judges a commit's closing keyword and logs its breadcrumb from candidate checkouts: the start, the main checkout, and the second walk's readings. It then takes the fresh commit whose subject matches the command's `-m` text. All of these are warn or log tier:

- **A5x:** a commit into a foreign repo after the loss gets no warning.
- **F6F:** with `-F <file>` or an editor message, the lone-fresh-commit fallback can judge another session's fresh commit, warning and logging the wrong breadcrumb.
- **F5amb:** when two checkouts both offer a commit with a matching subject, the real commit gets neither its warning nor its breadcrumb. Base gave both.
- **F7strip/F10cfg:** with `--cleanup=strip` or `-c commit.cleanup=strip` and a `#`-first `-m`, git's subject differs from the command text, so no warning is given.
- The sibling P1 layout logs an extra fallback breadcrumb with the worktree's old HEAD. It is noise; no consumer reads commit breadcrumbs.
- **Cost:** a lost commit spawns one `git log` per worktree, 13 spawns with 10 worktrees against base's 2.

## Deliverables

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build of #4303 (run 2026-10-25T143627-spec-4303), SDD Task 2 parked finding and final-review ruling

## Current State

In `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`, a NAME=value assignment prefix, an `env` prefix or a `sudo` prefix hides every write shape. Each of these resolves `[]`, while bash 3.2 and 5 write or commit in the main checkout:

- `X=1 cp a /main/f.js`
- `sudo cp a /main/f.js`
- `X=1 tee /main/f.js`
- `X=1 sed -i s/a/b/ /main/f.js`
- `cd M; x+=1 git commit -m x` and `x+=1 git -C M commit -m x`

A quoted name goes the other way. `"x"=1 cd /main` is read as an assignment plus a cd, but bash 3.2 and 5 run `x=1` as a command ("command not found") and stay put. That is a fail-open: from the main checkout, `"x"=1 cd /wt; cp a f.js` resolves only `/wt/f.js`, while bash writes the main checkout's `f.js`.

Compound keywords and the `builtin`/`command`/`pushd` prefixes are #4244's scope, not this record's. While in visitSegment, also replace the `while ((next = …) > cdLead)` assignment-in-condition loop (`git-command.js:~736`) with a plain loop.

2. Read a quoted-name assignment as bash does.
3. Pin each shape with its bash 3.2 and 5 verdicts.

- Every shape above resolves the path bash writes, so the write gate denies it from a worktree of a worktree-always repo.
- `"x"=1 cd /main` resolves no cd, so `"x"=1 cd /wt; cp a f.js` from the main checkout resolves the main checkout's `f.js`.

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js`'s `checkResumeFreshness` maps `fs.existsSync(worktree) === false` to `{ safe: true, verdict: 'worktree-gone' }`. `existsSync` also returns false on `EACCES`, `ELOOP` or `EIO`. So for an `interrupted` run, a recorded worktree path the probe cannot look at reads as gone, and the resume goes ahead.

The other resume caller, `plugin/bin/lib/flow/consolidated-pass.js`'s `parentLiveDetail`, gates the same case on path-guard's `lstatType(worktree).type === 'missing'`. That is true only for a clean `ENOENT`, so the two callers disagree on an unreadable path. #4420 left the line unchanged, because its spec kept the five pre-probe returns in their existing order.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `checkResumeFreshness` returns `worktree-gone` only when path-guard's `lstatType(worktree).type === 'missing'`. Any other unreadable result falls through to `runLiveness`, whose `error` entry `blocksResume` reads as `indeterminate`.
- [ ] The verdict-string set and the order of the five pre-probe returns stay unchanged.
- [ ] One equivalence row in the PR body: an unreadable worktree path of an `interrupted` run moves from `worktree-gone` (resume) to `indeterminate` (block).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An `interrupted` run whose recorded worktree path is a symlink loop (`ELOOP`) gets verdict `indeterminate`, not `worktree-gone`. The test is red on the current code.
2. An `interrupted` run whose recorded worktree path does not exist still gets `worktree-gone`.
3. `tests/path-guard-conformance.test.js`'s allowlist entry for `lib/hooks/resume-freshness.js` (`existsSync: 1`) is removed, and the suite passes.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Resuming an interrupted pipeline run no longer treats a worktree path it cannot read as deleted, so it waits instead of resuming over a possibly live run.

## Current State

#4285 added `tests/helpers/path-stub.js` (`STUB_SKIP`, `installStub`, `pathWithOnly`). It chose which tests skip on win32 from one Windows run's failing list. The rule the windows-checkout-test-parity skill now states is different: judge each test by whether it writes a stub and whether its assertion depends on that stub running. A failing list never shows a test that passes vacuously, so the two selections differ.

A scripted audit of the six installStub suites found 22 stub-installing tests with no `STUB_SKIP`. They are in `tests/reconcile.test.js` at 1463-1581 (reconcileWithAsyncMerge), 2961/2970/2995 (reconcileWithRecordedResolver) and 3125-3258 (the #4180 dryRunFixture group), plus `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/prune-remote.test.js:407` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` at 168/250/572/746/810. The stub never runs on windows-latest, so several of these pass vacuously. Their assertions are things only the stub can make true or false: `ghCalls() === ''`, `fetchCalls` deep-equal to `[]`, and the batch-fail fallback path. A review agent no-op'd the stub on reconcile 3125 and 1469 and on prune-remote 407, and each still printed `ok 1`. reap-merged 746/810 skip on a chmod reason (`MID_DELETE_SKIP`), not on `STUB_SKIP`.

Single-stub `gh` wrappers outside the helper still hand-roll the install, so their temp dirs leak and their win32 skip reasons differ: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` (105/141), `tests/console-execute.test.js:469`, `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js:523` and `tests/hooks-resolve-console.test.js:82`. In reap-merged.test.js:287 the stub is installed before a worktree-lock call that can throw, outside the try that restores it.

The helper's own pin suite has two gaps. `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js:86` is titled as a PATHEXT test, but the binary lookup never consults PATHEXT, and no case excludes a `gh.CMD`. The `STUB_SKIP` pin at :28 reduces to `=== false` off win32.

## Deliverables

- Go through the 22 tests one at a time. Add `{ skip: STUB_SKIP }` where the assertion depends on the stub running. Where a test keeps running on win32, add a comment saying its assertions hold whatever answers on PATH. reap-merged 746/810 skip with the stub reason when the stub is what fails there.
- Move the single-stub hand-rolled wrappers listed above onto `installStub` with `STUB_SKIP`. The multi-stub wrappers the parity skill names stay hand-rolled.
- Move reap-merged.test.js:287's stub install inside the try that restores it.
- In `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js`, retitle the :86 test to what the lookup actually does, add an excluded-`gh.CMD` case, and give the :28 pin a win32 assertion by injecting the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1.1: re-running the stub-dependence audit over the installStub suites reports no stub-installing test that lacks both `STUB_SKIP` and a comment explaining why it holds on win32.
- AC1.2: a `windows-regression.yml` run on the branch lists no newly failing file, and each test that newly skips reports `# SKIP win32: execFile resolves only .exe/.com on PATH, so a script stub is never spawned` in `verify-logs/tests.log`.
- AC2.1: none of the listed single-stub wrappers writes its own temp dir or PATH entry any more (a grep for `mkdtemp` beside `PATH =` in those files comes back empty).
- AC3.1: `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js` has a case where an excluded `gh.CMD` on PATH makes `pathWithOnly` exclude that directory, and a win32 `STUB_SKIP` assertion.

## Release Note

Internal: tests that fake `git`/`gh` now skip on Windows whenever their result depends on the fake running, instead of passing without testing anything.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `tests/reconcile.test.js` — STUB_SKIP on the stub-dependent tests
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/prune-remote.test.js` — STUB_SKIP on the batch-fail fallback test
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` — STUB_SKIP on stub-dependent tests; stub install inside the try
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — single-stub gh helpers onto installStub
- `tests/console-execute.test.js` — gh stub onto installStub
- `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` — gh stub onto installStub
- `tests/hooks-resolve-console.test.js` — gh stub onto installStub
- `tests/path-stub-helper.test.js` — retitle the PATHEXT test, add a gh.CMD exclude case and a win32 STUB_SKIP pin

Origin: reflect full from #3315
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/issues/claim-store.js`'s `tombstoneInFlightPr` is the only in-flight-PR check in `/flow`'s Step 2.8 claim (`plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js:454`). It runs only for a `pr-opened:` tombstone. A claim whose 72h TTL expired while its run was still mid-pipeline classifies `'stale'` and is re-claimed through a conditional write, with no PR check at all.

#3315 is the observed case. Dispatch's first call finished the build and opened draft PR #3927 (2026-10-22). The second call never ran, and the claim expired on 2026-10-25. A `/claude-tweaks:flow #3315` with `build` in the step list would have minted a fresh run, re-claimed the stale claim, and rebuilt from scratch alongside the open PR. `steps-and-gates.md`'s case-5 resume check only applies when `build` is absent from the step list. `/tidy`'s needs-decision comment on #3315 (2026-10-26) also proposed releasing the stale claim without naming the open PR. The 2026-10-26 run caught this only through a manual `gh pr list` before claiming.

## Deliverables

- In the stale branch of `claim-targets.js`, before the conditional write, look for an open PR that carries the stale claim's `runId` in its `claude-tweaks-run:` marker. When one exists, stop with the same in-flight card and resume routing the `pr-opened:` tombstone case already uses.
- `/tidy`'s stale-claim release proposal names an open marked PR when one exists, and recommends resuming its `### Resume` line rather than a plain release.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Release Note

`/flow` no longer starts a duplicate build for a record whose earlier run's claim expired while that run's draft PR was still open. It points you at the existing PR's resume command instead.

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/claim-store.js` — shared PR lookup beside tombstoneInFlightPr

Origin: reflect full from #4288

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Two pipeline gates read the same bookkeeping-only delta and reach opposite answers.
- `/claude-tweaks:test`'s Skip-if-recent (`plugin/skills/test/verification.md`) sees `VERIFICATION_SHA` ≠ HEAD. It classifies every changed path against `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json`, and when all of them are bookkeeping-only (`suites: []`) it skips verification and writes no stamp.
- `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 (`plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md`) then reads `verify.js --stamp-status`. It gets `verifiedHead: false`, because the full-pass stamp names the pre-ledger-commit SHA. Its gate row says "re-trigger `/claude-tweaks:test`, re-check", but the re-triggered `/test` takes the same bookkeeping-only skip and still writes no stamp, so the gate names no terminal outcome.
- A `/flow` run reaches this state whenever a bookkeeping-only commit lands between `/build` Common Step 5's full verify and `/test` (for example, run-ledger rows recording AC results, which only exist after verify). #4288's run hit it: build verified 65fd6e5, a ledger-only commit moved HEAD to 81a3dc6, and the review got past the gate only by hand-running a scoped `verify.js --scope .claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json --integration-branch origin/main` (`scope: none`, `still-verified: bookkeeping-only delta`), which wrote a `none` stamp verifying HEAD.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Make `/claude-tweaks:test`'s bookkeeping-only Skip-if-recent branch run the scoped `verify.js` invocation the Re-verify scoping table already gives the multi-spec spec-N step (`none` on a bookkeeping-only delta), so the skip leaves a stamp that verifies HEAD instead of writing nothing.
- [ ] Give `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5's `verifiedHead: false` row a terminal outcome: after one re-trigger, a still-unverified stamp either stops the review with a named cause or passes on a recorded bookkeeping-only classification. It must never loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a `/flow` run whose only change after build's full verify is the run ledger commit, `/claude-tweaks:test` exits Skip-if-recent with `verify.js --stamp-status` reporting `verifiedHead: true` (`scope: none`) at the new HEAD.
2. `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 then passes its test gate with no hand-run `verify.js` and no second `/test` re-trigger.
3. A delta with any non-bookkeeping path still runs the scoped or full re-verify exactly as today.

## Release Note

A pipeline run no longer stalls at the review test gate after build commits its own ledger: the test step's bookkeeping-only skip now leaves a verification stamp for the new commit.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — bookkeeping-only Skip-if-recent branch runs the scoped none-stamp verify
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 1.5 verifiedHead:false row gets a terminal outcome

Origin: dispatch close-out session 2026-10-26 (PRs #4276, #4302, #4319, #4334, #4354)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `localHasMerge` (the #1130 guard against #657) checks the merge commit against `refs/heads/{integration}`. When the local ref lacks it, the guard falls back to `origin/{integration}` (#2565).

That fallback also fires when the local integration branch exists but is behind. In that case the tracked `work/{n}-spec.md` is not in the main checkout yet. The sweep moves the run dir's gitignored half into `archive/` and has nothing to `git mv`.

Once main fast-forwards, the spec reappears at `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run}/work/` as a state-less dir. `archive-run` refuses it (no readable run-state.json). The orphaned-mint sweep only takes it after a 24 h TTL.

Observed 2026-10-26: the main checkout was dirty and 19 commits behind origin. Four stranded specs (runs for #3988/#3987/#3980/#3759) were the dirt that blocked mirror-ff. In that state, the merges of PRs #4276/#4302/#4319/#4334/#4354 stranded five more specs the same way, a self-perpetuating loop.

Both sets were archived by hand in 7b39e4683 and 9aaf50f45.

## Deliverables

1. Make the archive decision require the merge in the checkout the `git mv` runs against. Accept the local integration ref, or HEAD when that is the integration branch. When only `origin/{integration}` has it while the local ref exists and is behind, skip and retry on a later pass instead of archiving the untracked half.
2. Keep #2565's case working: a main checkout parked on another branch, or with no local integration ref.
3. Add a regression test in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`. It uses a local integration branch behind an origin that holds the merge, and asserts that nothing is moved and the reason is a retryable skip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a local integration branch behind the merge and origin holding it, reconcile leaves the run dir in place and reports a retryable skip.
- [ ] After the local branch fast-forwards, the same pass archives the run dir and `git mv`s `work/` in one commit.
- [ ] #2565's no-local-ref and parked-checkout cases still archive.

## Release Note

Reconcile no longer half-archives a merged run while the main checkout is behind, so its spec file is never left stranded.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #4025, #4354, #4168, #2986, #3014, #3013, #3469, #4304, #4343, #4395, #3905, #4345

Origin: reflect full from #4025

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

During #4025's review, PR #4354 was `DIRTY`, conflicting with main after #4168 landed, and had run no CI beyond the label workflows. The reviewer found the conflict by reading the PR state by hand, about 3 hours after the build opened the PR.

`bin/pr-checks.js` is the one read `/claude-tweaks:test`'s pipeline gate and `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 both run (`_shared/pr-check-gate.md`). Probed at HEAD, its `gh pr view` asks only for `headRefOid,statusCheckRollup,baseRefName` (`pr-checks.js:187`), and its states are `red | inherited-red | pending | stale | green | no-ci | read-failed | no-pr | gh-absent`. A conflicted PR with no check runs therefore reads `no-ci`, a fail-open `SKIP` ("local verification only"), or `pending` when the repo has pull_request CI (`classify.js:77`). The review gate table (`review/code-mode-steps.md:108-109`) proceeds on anything but `red`.

Premise correction: the plugin already detects a conflicted PR, but only at phase exits. `bin/pr-merge-state.js` (#2986) runs after every phase-exit push through `phase-exit.js`, classifies with an exported `classifyMergeState` (`pr-merge-state.js:63-69`, exported at `:148`: `DIRTY` or `CONFLICTING` is conclusive, `UNKNOWN` is no signal), and is routed by `_shared/git-discipline.md`'s Post-push merge-state check. The gap is a base that moves after the last phase-exit push. The next gate reads checks only, and the `--pr` display readers (`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`, `wrap-up/pack.js`, `dispatch/settle-parked.md`) count such a PR as `no-ci`. `bin/lib/flow/preflight.js:294-310` holds a third, inline `CONFLICTING` check (#3014).

## Deliverables

1. Add a `conflicting` state to `pr-checks.js`. Request `mergeable,mergeStateStatus` in its existing `gh pr view` call and classify with `pr-merge-state.js`'s `classifyMergeState`, moved to a shared lib module both CLIs import, not copied. Carry `mergeStateStatus`, `mergeable` and `baseBranch` (the PR's `baseRefName`) in the envelope.
2. Precedence: `conflicting` replaces every check-derived state (`red`, `inherited-red`, `pending`, `green`, `no-ci`), because a conflicted PR gets no new `pull_request` runs, so its checks say nothing about HEAD. `stale` still wins, because a local HEAD ahead of the PR may already hold the catch-up. `no-pr`, `gh-absent` and a failed `gh pr view` stay as they are. `unknown` merge state changes nothing.
3. Route `conflicting` in `_shared/pr-check-gate.md` by citing `_shared/git-discipline.md`'s Post-push merge-state check routing rather than restating it. In `auto`/`confirm`, run its Catch-up, then re-run the gate once. In `interactive`/`hybrid`, stop at the gate and give the catch-up commands. The CLI's own `--run` decisions.md line for `conflicting` is one `AUTO` entry naming the PR and base.
4. Add the `conflicting` row to `review/code-mode-steps.md`'s Step 1.5 gate table, citing `pr-check-gate.md`, and map the state in every `pr-checks.js --pr` reader: `_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s count (not a green or `no-ci` candidate), `wrap-up/pack.js` and `dispatch/settle-parked.md`.
5. Update `pr-checks.js`'s header comment, its USAGE state list, and `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s state list where they enumerate states.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture PR view with `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY` and no check runs classifies `conflicting`, not `no-ci`, `pending` or `green`. So does `mergeable: CONFLICTING` with `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`.
- `mergeStateStatus: UNKNOWN` with `mergeable: UNKNOWN` leaves the check-derived state unchanged.
- A `DIRTY` view whose `headRefOid` differs from local HEAD reads `stale`, not `conflicting`.
- `pr-merge-state.js`'s outputs are byte-identical on its existing tests after `classifyMergeState` moves, and both CLIs import the one function.
- Under `--run`, a `conflicting` read writes one `AUTO` `PR-check gate` entry. `--pr` writes nothing.
- `review/code-mode-steps.md`'s gate table and `pr-check-gate.md`'s routing name `conflicting`. Every `pr-checks.js --pr` reader maps it, so none treats it as green or `no-ci`.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The test and review gates now notice when a pull request has fallen into a merge conflict, so the run catches up instead of reviewing a branch that will never get CI.

## Technical Approach

Move `classifyMergeState` into `plugin/bin/lib/pr-checks/classify.js`, the classification lib `pr-checks.js` already imports, or into a small sibling module, and have `pr-merge-state.js` import it from there. Apply it in `classifyPr` after the rollup verdict, so the precedence rule in Deliverable 2 lives in one place. Routing stays in prose by citation: `pr-check-gate.md` points at `git-discipline.md`'s Post-push merge-state check and Catch-up for the action, so the two conflict routes cannot drift.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/pr-checks.js` — request merge fields; `conflicting` state; envelope; USAGE
- `plugin/bin/lib/pr-checks/classify.js` — shared `classifyMergeState`
- `plugin/bin/pr-merge-state.js` — import the moved classifier
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-check-gate.md` — route `conflicting`
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 1.5 gate row
- `plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md` — count mapping
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `ci.state` consumer
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-parked.md` — fresh CI read consumer
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — state list
- `tests/bin-lib/pr-checks/classify.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/pr-checks/cli.test.js` — classification, precedence and envelope cases
- `tests/bin-lib/pr-merge-state/cli.test.js` — unchanged outputs after the move

## Gotchas

- Auto-mode contract: a new mid-flow stop in `auto` is forbidden unless it is a HARD-GATE (`_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`). A merge conflict is not a test failure, so `auto` runs the catch-up instead of stopping. Only `interactive`/`hybrid` stop.
- GitHub computes mergeability asynchronously, so `UNKNOWN` is common right after a push. Never read it as a conflict and never re-read inside this CLI, the same rule `pr-merge-state.js` follows.
- Expand-contract: an installed build's prose may read an older `pr-checks.js`, and a newer CLI's `conflicting` may reach older prose that lacks the row. Older routing falls to its own default, which must not read it as green. Check each consumer's unknown-state fallback, and land the prose rows in the same release as the CLI state.
- `pr-checks.js`'s state list is enumerated in its header comment, its USAGE and `docs/plugin-structure.md`, and `pr-merge-state.js`'s `STATES` is pinned to prose by `tests/git-discipline-merge-state-conformance.test.js`. Find every enumeration with `git grep -n "no-ci | read-failed"` and update them together.
- `preflight.js`'s inline `CONFLICTING` check (#3014) is a third copy. Importing the shared classifier there is in scope only if it is a one-line swap with unchanged output, otherwise leave it.
- #4304 (catch-up before the whole-branch review) and #4343 (catch-up before build's final verification) add proactive catch-ups at other points. They narrow the window but do not remove it, because the base can still move after them, so this gate-time detection stays needed. #4395 edits the same Step 1.5 gate table (its `verifiedHead: false` row). Rebase onto whichever lands first.

## Original request

pr-checks.js cannot see a merge-conflicted PR: the review PR-check gate lets a DIRTY PR with no CI through

Origin: reflect full from #4025

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

During #4025's review, PR #4354 was `DIRTY` (a merge conflict with main after #4168 landed) and had run no CI beyond the label workflows. `bin/pr-checks.js` and `bin/lib/pr-checks/classify.js` classify only check runs (`red|pending|stale|green|no-ci|...`); nothing in them reads `mergeStateStatus`, so the review Step 1.5 PR-check gate cannot tell a clean PR from one that is conflicted and therefore never gets CI. The conflict was found only because the reviewer read the PR state by hand, ~3 hours after the build opened it.

## Deliverables

Make `pr-checks.js` report a conflicted PR (`mergeStateStatus` `DIRTY`, or `mergeable` `CONFLICTING`) as its own state, distinct from `no-ci`, with the conflicting base named.

Have review Step 1.5 (`review/code-mode-steps.md`) stop on that state with the catch-up instruction (`_shared/git-discipline.md`, Catching a branch up with main) instead of proceeding to the lenses.

## Acceptance Criteria

A fixture PR with `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY` and no check runs classifies as the new conflicted state, not `no-ci` or `green`.

The review gate table maps the conflicted state to a stop with the catch-up command.

## Release Note

A review now stops at once when its pull request has a merge conflict, instead of reviewing a branch that can never get CI.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/pr-checks/classify.js` — modify
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-check-gate.md` — modify

Surface: infra

**Related:** #1651, #3340, #4028, #347, #4283, #3822, #4217, #4345, #3978, #4125

Origin: upstream feedback from an unattended multi-spec `/flow` run's consolidated Review Console (#347)

## Current State

In a worktree-isolated session, `node <plugin>/bin/hooks.js spec-status --run <parent> --spec <n> --status complete --phase wrap-up` is refused with "runs a string through complete, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree". It is refused alone and as the second command after `;`. The workaround the reporter used was a `node -e` call that builds the word from parts.

Premise correction: this is not a regression of a #1651 fix. The refusal comes from the Claude Code harness's worktree-isolation guard, not from this plugin. #1651 could not change the guard, so it documented the shape and its workaround instead. `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` §7 lists "Literal token `complete` as an argument" as `refused`, last verified 2026-10-20 (#3340), with the composed-word `node -e` workaround. The documented completion call has used that composed form since #1651 (`plugin/skills/flow/multispec-progress-banner.md:22-26`, commit 11e73372b). `multispec-review-console.md`'s re-entry step 4 names no `spec-status` call. So the documented command works, and the run's refusal came from typing the plain form the docs warn against.

The real cost is that the only safe spelling of the most frequent multi-spec transition is a fragile one-liner. It holds a `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` splice inside `node -e` text and a hand-built argv, so an agent reaching for the plain command walks into the refusal first.

`hooks.js` reads flag values only in the spaced form. `flagVal` (`plugin/bin/hooks.js:216-219`) is `args.indexOf(name)` plus the next token, and `resolveRunArg` uses `args.indexOf('--run')` (`:405`). `firstUnknownFlag` (`:201`) treats any `--*` token not in `KNOWN_FLAGS` as unknown, so `--status=complete` is refused as an unknown flag today. The repo's own model of the guard says a shell word that only contains `complete` passes, and only a whole word `complete` is refused (`tools/guard-refusals/shapes.js:185-189`, the `complete-token` detector at `:387`). That predicts `--status=complete`, one shell word, passes the guard.

## Deliverables

1. Before any code change, probe in a real worktree-isolated session that `node /abs/plugin/bin/hooks.js spec-status --run /abs/parent --spec 1 --status=complete --phase wrap-up` is not refused by the guard, and that the spaced form still is. Record the result as a new `scratch-worktree.md` §7 row, or as a dated addition to the `complete`-token row, with the date and record number.
2. If the probe passes, teach `hooks.js` the `--flag=value` form for every flag in `VALUE_FLAGS`, uniformly across `flagVal`, `firstUnknownFlag` and `resolveRunArg`'s `--run` lookup, so one rule covers every verb rather than `spec-status` alone. The spaced form keeps working unchanged.
3. Replace the composed `node -e` completion call in `multispec-progress-banner.md` with the plain `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hooks.js" spec-status … --status=complete …` form, and point the §7 `complete`-token row's workaround at it for `hooks.js` callers.
4. If the probe shows the guard refuses `--status=complete` too, stop at Deliverable 1. Record the finding in §7 and leave the code and the banner doc unchanged. A different spelling then needs its own decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- §7 carries the probed verdict for `--status=complete`, dated, from a real worktree-isolated session.
- On the passing path, `hooks.js spec-status … --status=complete …` and `--status complete` produce the same `manifest.yml` transition and banner. So do `--run=<dir>` and `--run <dir>`, and `--spec=<n>` and `--spec <n>`.
- An undeclared `--bogus=x` is still refused by the unknown-flag guard, and `--status=` with an empty value is a usage error, not a silent empty status.
- The `complete-token` detector (`tools/guard-refusals/shapes.js:387`) does not flag the new banner fence, so `tests/skill-fence-guard-shapes.test.js` passes, and its frozen fixture (`tests/fixtures/guard-refusals/banned-shapes.md`, `--status complete`) is still flagged.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Multi-spec `/flow` runs in a worktree can mark a spec finished with a plain `spec-status --status=complete` command instead of a composed `node -e` workaround.

## Technical Approach

Parse `--name=value` once, in a small helper used by `flagVal`, `firstUnknownFlag` and `resolveRunArg`: split on the first `=` when the name part is a declared value flag. Keep `VALUE_FLAGS` as the single list of flags that take a value. A parse-on-every-call shim in `runSpecStatus` alone would leave the other verbs inconsistent, so it is the wrong place.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `flagVal`, `firstUnknownFlag`, `resolveRunArg`, `VALUE_FLAGS`
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-progress-banner.md` — the completion call
- `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` — §7 `complete`-token row
- `tests/hooks-spec-status.test.js` — `=` form parity
- `tests/hooks-help-guard.test.js` — unknown-flag guard with the `=` form
- `tools/guard-refusals/shapes.js` — reference only (`complete-token` detector)

## Gotchas

- The probe needs a session whose worktree guard is live. A main-checkout session does not run the harness's worktree-isolation guard, so a pass there proves nothing.
- The harness guard is outside this repo and changes between builds (see §7's "refused in … passes now" rows). Pin the probe's date, and expect a later build to change the verdict either way.
- Conformance tests pin the banner doc's prose, including `node -e` snippet syntax (commit 11e73372b, refs #1651), `tests/timing-prose-conformance.test.js` and `tests/flow-mixed-execution-convention.test.js`. Run the full suite after the doc edit, not only the hooks tests.
- Expand-contract: the installed build reads this repo's prose with older code. A session on a build without `=` parsing that reads the new banner doc would hit the unknown-flag refusal. Land the parser in a release before, or in the same release as, the doc switch, and note it in the release.
- #4283 (ready) covers skill snippets that splice `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` into JS string literals, which breaks on a backslash Windows root. Deliverable 3 removes one such splice from `multispec-progress-banner.md`, so rebase whichever lands second and drop the banner snippet from #4283's scope if it lists it.

## Original request

Worktree Bash guard again refuses spec-status --status complete (regression of #1651, 6.153.0)

Regression of #1651 on plugin 6.153.0.

In a worktree-isolated session, the Bash guard refuses the documented multi-spec completion call:

```
node <plugin>/bin/hooks.js spec-status --run <parent-run-dir> --spec 812 --status complete --phase wrap-up
```

The refusal message is "this command runs a string through complete, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree". The guard reads the argument value `complete` as the bash builtin `complete`. The same refusal appears when the call is the second command after `;`, and when it is the only command in the Bash call. `--status=complete` is not accepted by `spec-status`'s parser, so the spelled-out form is the only documented one (`flow/multispec-progress-banner.md`, `flow/multispec-review-console.md` re-entry step 4).

**Impact:** an in-worktree multi-spec `/flow` run cannot mark a spec finished through the documented command, which leaves the manifest stale and blocks the consolidated pass's eligibility check.

**Workaround used:** `node -e "require('child_process').execFileSync(process.execPath,[hooks,'spec-status',...,'--status','comp'+'lete',...])"`.

**Expected:** the guard treats `complete` as an argument when it is not in command position (the #1651 fix), or `spec-status` also accepts `--status=complete`.

_Filed from an unattended overnight `/flow #812,#813` run's consolidated Review Console (unattended ceiling files upstream feedback, #347)._

**Related:** #4212, #4210, #4247

Origin: dispatch close-out of PR #4223 (record #4212), 2026-10-25

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

After #4210 (PR #4235, merge `b4a2f59db`), `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s `tokenize` returns a per-character `spanKinds` mask and keeps backslashes in token values as typed; `isUnresolvable` then rejects any token still carrying a backslash. Measured on main (2026-10-25) against #4212's test expectations, three classes resolve **no** target where bash writes to a concrete path. All three are fail-open: none fabricates a target.

1. **Escaped blank in a path word:** `mkdir a\ b`, `mkdir -p /r/a\ b/c`, `cp a my\ file.js`, `cd /r/a\ b && git commit -m x` return `[]`; bash targets `/r/a b`, `/r/a b/c`, `/r/my file.js`, `/r/a b`.
2. **Backslash-newline line continuation** inside or before a word: `echo x >/ma\<newline>in/x` and `mkdir -p \<newline>/abs/dir` return `[]`; bash targets `/main/x` and `/abs/dir`.
3. **A `$` / `${…}` / backtick word, then an escaped blank, then `>`:** `echo $M\ >x`, `echo ${M}\ >x`, ``echo `d`\ >x``, `echo $M\ bar>x` return `[]`; bash redirects to `x`. `echo $M>x` staying `[]` is the documented gap and must not change.

PR #4223 (record #4212, branch `worktree-dispatch-record-4212`, tip `9a6fc75a9`) implemented all three by unescaping values in the old regex tokenizer. It was closed unmerged: it predates the span mask, conflicts with it in all four touched files, and lacks #4210's quoted-span and `(ls)>out` resolution. #4212's own acceptance criteria already pass on main.

## Deliverables

- `tokenize` yields the unescaped value for an escaped blank in a bare word and for an escaped double quote, and deletes a backslash-newline pair before word splitting, while keeping `spanKinds[i].length === tokens[i].length` (the mask must shrink with the value) and keeping every other backslash pair verbatim (Windows paths, `\'`).
- The glued-redirect scan resolves the operand after an escaped blank that follows a `$`/backtick prefix (`$M\ >x`), without accepting `$M>x`.
- `isUnresolvable` stops rejecting a token whose only backslashes were unescaped by the tokenizer.
- `docs/journeys/write-a-glued-redirect-from-the-main-checkout-4015.md` and the redirect paragraph in `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` describe the new behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every case listed in Current State resolves the bash target named there, pinned in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` / `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js`, each going red when the change is reverted.
- #4212's carried-over expectations hold on the new code: `echo "a\" b>c "` → none, `echo foo>x` → `x`, `echo foo\\>x` → `x`, `echo foo\>x` → none, `cd \'/wt\' && git commit` → none, `echo x > \'/abs/f\'` → none, `echo $M>x` → none, and `echo a\"b>c` → `c` (bash's actual target; #4212 had pinned it as a known miss).
- #4210's cases still resolve (`echo "hi">x` → `x`, `(ls)>out` → `out`), and the existing `fileWriteTargets` / `gitTargets` / `mkdirTargets` suites pass unchanged.
- Full `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate now sees writes to a path with an escaped space, a path split by a line continuation, and a redirect after a `$VAR\ ` word, which it previously let through.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — modify
- `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` — modify
- `docs/journeys/write-a-glued-redirect-from-the-main-checkout-4015.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` — modify

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3813, #4125, #4162

Origin: #3950 final whole-branch review, finding I2 (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:tidy`'s console backfill mode (`plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md`, CLI `plugin/bin/console-backfill.js`) settles Review Console residue left in archived runs: it files records, posts digest lines, and rewrites each `console.json`. Its filing and digest steps go through GitHub Issues only (`gh issue create`, `gh issue comment` on the digest issue), so Step 3's backend gate stops any project whose `work-backend` is not `github-issues` with:

`HELD — console backfill needs work-backend: github-issues; local-files support is tracked as the backlog record "Console backfill: settle Review Console residue under work-backend: local-files"`

A `work-backend: local-files` project therefore keeps every unreviewed console item forever, and its session-start residue notice never clears except by a blanket `console-residue.js --ack-all`.

## Deliverables

- Console backfill runs under `work-backend: local-files`: filings become local record files through the same writer `/claude-tweaks:capture` uses under that backend, and digest lines append to the local digest the materiality floor names for that backend (`_shared/materiality-floor.md`).
- Filing dedup (claim fingerprint and `consolebackfill-item` marker) and digest dedup read the local records and local digest, so the crash-resume guarantees hold as they do on GitHub.
- Step 3's backend gate passes `local-files`; the HELD line is removed or narrowed to backends that remain unsupported, and its pin in `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js` is updated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a `local-files` fixture project with one archived run holding a confirmed finding, a digest-bound finding and a dismissal, a backfill pass leaves one local record, one local digest line, and a `console.json` whose items all carry a `ref`.
- A second pass over the same fixture writes nothing.
- A pass interrupted after the record write and resumed after a claim-text change reuses that record rather than writing a second one.

## Release Note

Console backfill now settles Review Console residue in projects that keep work records as local files.

## Technical Approach

The CLI already plans from data the procedure hands it, so most of the change belongs in the procedure. `console-backfill.js dispose` takes `--existing` (today a `gh issue list --state all --json number,title,body` array) and `--digest-comments` (the digest issue's comment objects) (`plugin/bin/console-backfill.js:10-22`). Under `local-files`, the procedure builds `--existing` from `queryRecords` (`bin/lib/issues/local-store.js`) mapped to the same `{number,title,body}` shape, and passes the current `specs/digest.md` body as the digest input. `_shared/materiality-floor.md:70` already names that body a trusted single-writer string. Filing uses `createRecord`, the writer `/claude-tweaks:capture` uses under `local-files` (`plugin/skills/capture/SKILL.md:306-310`), and never `allocateId` + `writeRecord`. Digest lines append to `specs/digest.md` (`_shared/materiality-floor.md:158`).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md` — backend gate and filing/digest steps
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js` — filing and digest planning
- `plugin/bin/console-backfill.js` — `dispose` inputs (`--existing`, `--digest-comments`) for the local-files shapes
- `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js` — HELD-line pin (`:55`)
- `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill-dispose.test.js` — local-files planning cases

## Gotchas

- Under `local-files`, a record file and `specs/digest.md` are tracked files. Each landed write needs a commit, which the GitHub path never needs, so the procedure must run in a worktree and commit per write. Otherwise a crash leaves an uncommitted record that the next pass's `queryRecords` still sees. That is fine for dedup, but it must be committed before `console.json` cites it.
- A local record's ref is its id, not `#N` under a GitHub repo. Check that `apply`'s `ref` field and the residue reader (`lib/console/residue.js`) accept the local ref form before the console item is marked settled.
- The digest dedup input differs by backend: comment objects with author association on GitHub, a trusted file body on local-files (`_shared/materiality-floor.md:63-70`). `heldDigestComment` in `backfill-dispose.js` must take the local form without treating it as an untrusted comment.
- The HELD line is pinned verbatim in `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js:55` and also names this record by title. Update both when narrowing the gate.

## Original request

Console backfill: settle Review Console residue under work-backend: local-files

Origin: #3950 final whole-branch review, finding I2 (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:tidy`'s console backfill mode (`plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md`, CLI `plugin/bin/console-backfill.js`) settles Review Console residue left in archived runs: it files records, posts digest lines, and rewrites each `console.json`. Its filing and digest steps go through GitHub Issues only (`gh issue create`, `gh issue comment` on the digest issue), so Step 3's backend gate stops any project whose `work-backend` is not `github-issues` with:

`HELD — console backfill needs work-backend: github-issues; local-files support is tracked as the backlog record "Console backfill: settle Review Console residue under work-backend: local-files"`

A `work-backend: local-files` project therefore keeps every unreviewed console item forever, and its session-start residue notice never clears except by a blanket `console-residue.js --ack-all`.

## Deliverables

- Console backfill runs under `work-backend: local-files`: filings become local record files through the same writer `/claude-tweaks:capture` uses under that backend, and digest lines append to the local digest the materiality floor names for that backend (`_shared/materiality-floor.md`).
- Filing dedup (claim fingerprint and `consolebackfill-item` marker) and digest dedup read the local records and local digest, so the crash-resume guarantees hold as they do on GitHub.
- Step 3's backend gate passes `local-files`; the HELD line is removed or narrowed to backends that remain unsupported, and its pin in `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js` is updated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a `local-files` fixture project with one archived run holding a confirmed finding, a digest-bound finding and a dismissal, a backfill pass leaves one local record, one local digest line, and a `console.json` whose items all carry a `ref`.
- A second pass over the same fixture writes nothing.
- A pass interrupted after the record write and resumed after a claim-text change reuses that record rather than writing a second one.

## Release Note

Console backfill now settles Review Console residue in projects that keep work records as local files.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md` — backend gate and filing/digest steps
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js` — filing and digest planning
- `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js` — HELD-line pin

Origin: reflect full from #3947

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

A skill step that dispatches agents or calls CLIs is specified in prose, and nothing at spec, plan or authoring time asks what happens when each of those calls fails.

In #3947 (Step 3.7, `plugin/skills/review/step3-tiebreak.md`), the SDD final review needed 1 Critical and 6 Important fixes, and the later 4-lens review found 23 more findings. Most of them were the same kind of gap: what the reviewer does when a dispatch fails or returns non-DONE, when `write-findings` exits 2, when `resolve-tiebreak` crashes, or when `log-decision.js` fails. Each was added after the fact, across fix commits a2d09600d, a645f740b, cc098dd27 and 494bb6045.

`docs/skill-authoring.md` and `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` have no rule or check that asks for a failure path per external call.

## Deliverables

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` gains a rule: a step whose prose dispatches an agent or runs a CLI states, for each such call, its next move on failure (retry once / fallback rung / surface and stop) and the log line it writes.
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` gains a check: a plan task that adds or changes such a step carries a failure-path table (call → failure mode → next move → log line) before its prose is written.
- A conformance test pins both texts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/skill-authoring.md` contains the failure-path rule and names the three next-move kinds.
2. `plan-authoring-checks.md` contains the failure-path table check and its trigger (a task touching a step that dispatches an agent or runs a CLI).
3. A test asserts both, and it was shown to go red without each text.

## Release Note

Skill steps that dispatch agents or run tools now have to say up front what happens when each call fails, so those gaps are found while planning instead of in review.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — add the failure-path rule
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — add the failure-path table check

## Current State

After #3877, `/tidy`'s `## Arm ready PR` action (`plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md`) holds a record-linked PR whose acceptance labeling never landed. That covers three cases: the run's `verify.json` `acceptance-labeling` row is not `pass`/`skip`, no `demo:pending` is set on its `Fixes` records, and no trusted brief/try-it run comment exists. In those cases the action logs a `SKIP` to `decisions.md` instead of arming.

`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s `repo-wide` item 9 still classifies that same PR as a granted `[pr-unarmed]` candidate on every sweep. So `tidy/step-6-auto.md` re-stages the same record-linked "Arm ready PR" row each run, and a human approves an arm that only holds again. `step-6-auto.md`'s own header treats a recurring staged item as a missing routing rule.

## Deliverables

- Item 9 (or tidy's Step 6 routing) applies the same acceptance-labeling landed check as the arm action. It reuses `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3's live-state precheck: `demo:pending` on every `Fixes` record, or a trusted brief/try-it run comment. Where a local run dir resolves, it also reads that run's `verify.json` `acceptance-labeling` row.
- A not-landed record-linked PR routes to **Yours**, carrying the paste-ready recommendation the arm action already names: `/claude-tweaks:dispatch close-out #{record}`, or the no-run-dir alternative. It does not appear as an Arm ready PR row.
- The arm action's own guard stays as the execution-time backstop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A record-linked unarmed PR whose labeling has not landed surfaces under Yours with `/claude-tweaks:dispatch close-out #{record}` (or the no-run-dir alternative), not as an Arm ready PR row.
2. A record-linked PR whose labeling has landed still stages as an Arm ready PR row.
3. Housekeeping-marker PRs are unaffected.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

`/tidy` no longer keeps offering to arm a PR it will only hold for missing acceptance labeling.

- `plugin/skills/tidy/step-6-auto.md` — routes the not-landed record-linked flavor to Yours

Surface: infra

**Related:** #1426, #3900, #3901, #3902, #3904

## Current State

The materiality-floor digest (#1426) promoted nine below-floor findings in the `code-health` area into this record. All nine concern `/claude-tweaks:code-health` candidate generators, the deterministic pre-filters whose output an LLM judge then reads, so each is a precision or recall gap in a screen, not a user-visible defect. Each finding was filed with a trigger condition describing when it would start to matter. Verified against `origin/main` at shaping time:

**experiment-cleanup (1 item).** `normalizeBranch` in `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-experiment-cleanup.js` strips comments with literal-blind regexes (`/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g` and `/\/\/[^\n]*/g`), so a branch body holding `//` inside a string loses the rest of that line. Both compared sides are mangled alike, so impact is small. The regex-aware comment stripper from #3585 exists only as a test helper (`tests/helpers/strip-comments.js`), not under `plugin/bin/lib/`. (Defer-reason at filing: pre-existing-outside-diff.)

**scale-readiness (7 items), all in `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-scale-readiness.js`** unless noted:
1. A capitalized-receiver `X.find(` matches some in-memory constant lookups with a non-function argument, and a filtered `Model.find` with no `.limit` reads as unbounded. (genuinely-larger)
2. `findMany(args)` with a non-literal argument, a spread-only `{ ...opts }`, or a computed `['take']` key reads as unbounded. (genuinely-larger)
3. A module-scope object literal holding a client in a route file (`module.exports = { db: new PrismaClient() }`) reads as `per-request-db-client`, a shape the criteria fragment's What NOT to flag already names. (genuinely-larger)
4. `unbounded-pool` matches non-DB `Pool` classes (generic-pool, undici, workerpool), because it has no DB-dependency gate. The generator already holds `ctx.deps` for its cache and monitoring checks. (needs-human-decision)
5. `window.fetch(` / `globalThis.fetch(` third-party calls on the request path are not matched, because of the dotted-receiver lookbehind. (needs-human-decision)
6. `isRouteFile` is a pure path predicate, while real route membership also needs a server/data dependency or a `"use server"` directive. This is a naming trap for a future second caller; the definition carries a comment saying so. (needs-human-decision)
7. Nuxt, h3, @trpc/server and Elysia apps with only a framework dependency read as not applicable, because `SERVER_DEPS`/`DATA_DEPS` do not name them. (needs-human-decision)

**scale-readiness criteria fragment (1 item).** `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-scale-readiness.md`'s severity calibration leaves `unbounded-pool` off-serverless and an AI inline-slow-work call on a non-user-facing route unplaced, and its "bounded input" What NOT to flag line is in mild tension with a Severity "low" line. The judge falls back to holistic severity. (needs-human-decision)

## Deliverables

1. **Mechanical fixes, implemented with regression tests**, for the items whose fix is unambiguous:
   - experiment-cleanup: make `normalizeBranch` string-literal-aware. Promote the #3585 stripper from `tests/helpers/strip-comments.js` into `plugin/bin/lib/` and have both the test helper and the generator use it.
   - scale-readiness item 4: gate `unbounded-pool` on a declared DB dependency (`ctx.deps` against `DATA_DEPS`).
   - scale-readiness item 3: exclude the module-scope client shape already named in the fragment's What NOT to flag.
2. **Decision items surfaced, not decided unilaterally.** Items 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 and the criteria-fragment calibration were deferred as genuinely-larger or needs-human-decision. For each, the build either implements a fix with tests or records a one-line won't-fix or keep-deferred ruling with its reason. Every needs-human-decision ruling is staged for the human at the run's Review Console, never auto-applied.
3. Each of the nine promoted digest entry lines in #1426 carries `→ #3903`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `normalizeBranch` given two branch bodies that differ only after a `//` inside a string literal treats them as different, and given bodies that differ only in a real `//` comment treats them as equal. A test pins both, and reverting turns it red.
- The comment stripper lives under `plugin/bin/lib/`, and `tests/helpers/strip-comments.js` re-exports or wraps it, so there is one implementation.
- A project with a `new Pool(` from `generic-pool` (or `undici`/`workerpool`) and no DB dependency produces no `unbounded-pool` candidate, while a `pg` `new Pool(` with no `max` still does. Both are tested.
- A route file whose only DB client is held in a module-scope object literal produces no `per-request-db-client` candidate (tested).
- The closing PR, or the run's Review Console staging, states a disposition for every one of the nine items.
- Each of the nine digest entry lines in #1426 carries `→ #3903`.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Code-health's scale-readiness and experiment-cleanup screens raise fewer false candidates for non-database pools, module-scope clients and comment-like text inside strings.

## Technical Approach

Treat this as three independent slices: the stripper promotion plus `normalizeBranch`; the scale-readiness mechanical fixes (items 3 and 4); and the decision items. The decision items need no code unless a ruling chooses to fix. The `code-health-focus-vertical` and `bin-source-scan-conformance` project skills govern generator anatomy and the shared comment stripper's contract (including its stripper-verdict check), so read both before moving the stripper. Real-input fixtures matter more than synthetic ones for generator changes. Use a fixture that reproduces each false positive rather than a hand-built minimal string.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-experiment-cleanup.js` — `normalizeBranch`
- `tests/helpers/strip-comments.js` — the #3585 stripper, to be promoted
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-scale-readiness.js` — `unbounded-pool` gate, module-scope client exclusion, decision items 1/2/5/6/7
- `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-scale-readiness.md` — severity calibration (decision item)
- `tests/bin-lib/code-health/` — regression fixtures

## Gotchas

- `tests/helpers/strip-comments.js` is imported by the source-scan conformance suites. Moving it must keep every existing import path working, or the conformance suites lose their stripper silently.
- Five of the nine items were deferred as needs-human-decision. A headless build must stage those rulings rather than settle them; only the three mechanical fixes are unambiguous.
- Candidate generators are screens that the judge filters afterwards. A fix that over-narrows a pattern trades a false positive for a missed real finding, so pair every exclusion with a still-flagged positive case.

## Original request

## Current State
The materiality-floor digest (#1426) has accumulated 9 below-floor findings in the `code-health` area. Each was too small to file on its own, but together they make a coherent unit of work.

## Deliverables
- normalizeBranch strips comments with literal-blind regexes, so a compared branch body holding a // inside a string loses the rest of that line; both sides are mangled alike, so impact is small. Named in the fragment's What NOT to flag. - scale-readiness: `unbounded-pool` matches non-DB Pool classes (generic-pool, undici, workerpool) because it has no DB-dependency gate; gating on ctx.deps is the fix. groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: reflect full from #3783
**Related:** #205, #3783, #3740, #3508, #3706, #3721, #3905, #3936, #3946, #3963, #3973, #3974, #3975, #3976, #3977, #3979, #3982

## Current State

`plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` treats `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` (the sub-issues a run is closing, which the parent gate counts as `CLOSED` while they are still open) as a prose contract. A table (around line 195) tells each sub-issue-side caller what to pass:

| Caller | Set it passes |
|---|---|
| wrap-up Phase 4 execution | the one sub-issue this run is closing |
| wrap-up auto-merge short-circuit | the one sub-issue this run is closing |
| dispatch group auto-merge gate (`settle-and-merge.md`) | every member of the group (the merge carries one `Fixes #{issue}` per record) |
| dispatch close-out step 3 (`close-out.md:77`) | the PR's `Fixes` record numbers |

Ruling #205 kept this as prose while three callers existed and set "a fourth sub-issue-side caller" as the revisit condition. #3783 (PR #3869) added the fourth (close-out step 3), and the file now defers the decision to this record. An omitted set defaults to `{the sub-issue in hand}`, so the silent-no-op mode is closed, but nothing checks a wrong non-empty set: a caller that passes the wrong records labels the wrong parent's gate.

Every row is a different description of one fact: the records the merge closes. Under `pr-first` that is the PR's `Fixes` lines, which GitHub reports as the PR's `closingIssuesReferences`. `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` already reads that field (around line 320). Under `local-merge`/`current-branch` it is the wrap-up pack's `inputs.closingRecords` (`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `closingRecords`), the same set the carrier commit's `Fixes` lines are composed from.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Ruling recorded in `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`: `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` is **derived, not passed**. A shared helper computes it from the merge's own closing references, and the per-caller table becomes a description of that derivation.
- [ ] A `plugin/bin/` CLI (e.g. `closing-set.js`) returns the set as JSON: `--pr {n}` reads the PR's `closingIssuesReferences` (reusing `archive-merged.js`'s fetch shape); `--run {dir}` reads `wrap-up-pack.json`'s `inputs.closingRecords` for a run with no PR. An unreadable source exits non-zero with a reason and never prints `[]` as if nothing closes.
- [ ] All four callers call it instead of composing the set by hand: wrap-up Phase 4 execution (`execution-and-verification.md`), the auto-merge short-circuit (`auto-merge-short-circuit.md`), dispatch's group gate (`settle-and-merge.md`), and dispatch close-out step 3 (`close-out.md`)
- [ ] On a helper failure, keep today's default of `{the sub-issue in hand}`, and log the failure so the degraded set is visible
- [ ] A gh-absent (MCP transport) path, per `.claude/skills/mcp-agent-fetch-node-compute`: the agent fetches the PR's closing references through MCP and the helper reads them from a JSON file

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests: a PR whose body closes `#1` and `#2` yields `[1, 2]`; a `--run` dir whose pack lists `[7]` yields `[7]`; a failed PR read and a missing pack each exit non-zero with a reason and print no set
- A conformance test asserts each of the four caller files invokes the helper and none composes `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` by hand
- `verification-brief-parent-gate.md` carries the new ruling, keeps the `{the sub-issue in hand}` default as the failure fallback, and no longer defers to this record
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Parent acceptance gates compute which sub-issues a merge closes the same way at every merge site.

## Technical Approach

The original question was a helper versus prose with a new revisit condition. The trade-off it named, a helper "adds a code path every caller threads through" while "prose leaves a wrong non-empty set uncaught", only favors prose if the helper merely takes what the caller hands it. A helper that **derives** the set from the merge's own closing references removes the wrong-value risk entirely: the set equals what GitHub (or the carrier commit) will close, which is the definition the table was approximating. That is what makes the threading cost worth paying, and it also covers a fifth caller by construction instead of by a table row it might misread.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/closing-set.js` — new CLI
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/closing-set.js` (or a sibling module) — derivation with an injectable runner
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — existing `closingIssuesReferences` read to reuse or extract
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `closingRecords` (local-merge source)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — ruling and table
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — Acceptance labeling bullet
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md` — its `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` line (around line 110)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — group gate
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md` — step 3
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI

## Gotchas

- The group gate labels **before** the merge lands, so `closingIssuesReferences` must be read from the open PR's body, not from a merged-PR event; confirm it is populated on an open draft PR whose body carries `Fixes #N` lines.
- `closingIssuesReferences` only lists same-repo issues linked by a closing keyword. A record the PR fixes without the keyword is not in the set, so that case keeps today's behavior: the gate sees it as still open.
- If extracting the shared read from `archive-merged.js`, follow `.claude/skills/shared-contract-extraction`'s migration discipline so reconcile's behavior is unchanged.

## Original request

Decide #205 revisit — shared helper for CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES now that four callers pass it

Origin: reflect full from #3783

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` keeps `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` (the sub-issues a run is closing, read by the Self-inclusion rule) as a prose contract: each sub-issue-side caller reads the table there and passes its own set. Ruling #205 kept it prose while three callers existed and said to revisit it as a real code change once a fourth caller was added.

#3783 (PR #3869) added that fourth caller: `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3 now runs `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 1 with `CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` = the PR's `Fixes` records when a parked PR's labeling never landed. The parent-gate file now records that the condition is met and defers the decision to this record.

Nothing checks the value a caller passes: a wrong non-empty set labels the wrong records, which the default-to-the-sub-issue-in-hand rule does not catch.

## Deliverables

- A decision, recorded in `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`, on whether the closing set moves into a shared helper (for example a function that derives it from a PR's `Fixes` lines or a dispatch group) or stays a prose table.
- If a helper: every sub-issue-side caller (wrap-up Phase 4 execution, the auto-merge short-circuit, dispatch's group gate, dispatch close-out step 3) calls it, and a test pins each caller's use.
- If prose: the ruling states the new revisit condition.

## Open Question

Should `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` become a shared helper now that four callers pass it, or stay a prose table with a new revisit condition? A helper adds a code path every caller threads through; prose leaves a wrong non-empty set uncaught.

## Release Note

Parent acceptance gates compute which sub-issues a merge closes the same way at every merge site.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — record the #205 revisit decision
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md` — fourth caller passing CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES
