groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3809
**Related:** #3973, #3736, #3744, #3822, #3876, #3900, #3915, #3974, #3975, #3978, #3979, #3983, #3989

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's **Resolve now** bullet (line 127) carries a multi-run chase. A conflict resolution during a multi-run `local-merge` reconciliation ends in a `git commit`, and E1 (`runInner`'s tail loop in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) checks every commit against `ctx.runDir`, the newest non-terminal run in the project regardless of owner (`docs/hooks.md`'s "Two resolutions, not one"). The main checkout (or, under `worktree-always`, the scratch worktree the resolution runs in) is not any run's assigned worktree, so E1 denies unless the caller's ownership classifies as `foreign`, and the reconciling session usually owns the sibling runs. The procedure therefore closes this branch's run, then each other reconciliation branch's run E1 names in turn, and re-protects each one when the resolution lands or is abandoned.

That bullet drew #3809's whole-branch review Important 1, part of fix round 1, and four `/review` findings (3c at `:126` reproduced, plus single-agent 3b `:126`, 3c `:139`, 3f `:138`). The prose is correct today but is the most fragile part of the procedure, and it exists only because E1 cannot tell that a commit is concluding a merge of a live run's branch. E1's own deny message already names that case as legitimate ("If this checkout is intentionally correct (e.g. finishing the branch), clear the assignment first").

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a live-query exemption to E1, of the same shape as `isIntegrationBranchFastForwardPush` (#2542): a `commit` target is allowed when its checkout has a merge in progress (a `MERGE_HEAD` exists) **and** every commit `MERGE_HEAD` lists equals the current `HEAD` of a live run's worktree (`ctx.runState.worktree` or any entry in E1's existing `otherWorktrees` map). Log a new `wd-merge-finish` event (expected, actual, merged run dir) to `ctx.runDir` and allow.
- [ ] Every unprovable answer keeps today's E1 verdict (no exemption): no readable `MERGE_HEAD`, a `MERGE_HEAD` commit matching no live run's worktree `HEAD`, a run worktree whose `HEAD` cannot be read (removed worktree, git failure, timeout), or a target action other than `commit`
- [ ] Simplify `worktree-merge.md` step 5's Resolve-now bullet: drop the E1 chase (closing and re-protecting other reconciliation branches' runs) and keep the per-branch close-run ordering #3809 pinned (this branch's run closed first, re-protected after a step 4 failure)
- [ ] Document the exemption in `docs/hooks.md` beside E1's posture bullets

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`, a `git commit` in a checkout whose `MERGE_HEAD` equals a live sibling run's worktree `HEAD` is allowed and logs `wd-merge-finish`, while `ctx.runDir` names a different (newer) run
- The same commit is still denied when `MERGE_HEAD` is absent, when it names a commit that is no live run's worktree `HEAD`, when one of several `MERGE_HEAD` lines matches no live run, and when the matching run's worktree `HEAD` cannot be read. Each is its own test case.
- A `git push` or non-commit action is unaffected by the exemption
- Each new allow test goes red when the exemption is reverted (`git checkout --` on `pre-tool-use.js` only)
- `worktree-merge.md`'s Resolve-now bullet no longer instructs closing or re-protecting other branches' runs, and the existing #3809 ordering pins still pass
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Resolving a merge conflict during a multi-run local-merge reconciliation no longer has to close other branches' runs first.

## Technical Approach

The decision between the three signals the original request listed:

- **A run-state marker set and cleared by the reconciliation** was rejected. It adds a lifecycle (set before the merge, cleared on land or abandon) that the chase itself shows is fragile, and a marker left behind by a crash is a standing allow for that run's commits in the wrong checkout.
- **Narrowing E1's owner-unfiltered newest-run resolution in the main checkout** was rejected. The reconciling session usually owns the runs it merges, so their ownership verdict is `'mine'` and E1 would still deny. Narrowing further would also loosen E1 for the wrong-checkout commit it exists to catch.
- **A `MERGE_HEAD`-keyed live query** was chosen. Git already records the fact E1 lacks: a merge commit in progress whose parent-to-be is a live run's branch tip is that branch being integrated, not that run's work landing in the wrong checkout. It needs no new state, cannot go stale (git removes `MERGE_HEAD` when the merge concludes or aborts), and covers the `worktree-always` path too, where the resolution commits inside a scratch worktree that no run is assigned to.

Implementation follows `.claude/skills/pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions`: read `MERGE_HEAD` via `git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD` in the target's toplevel (a linked worktree's git dir differs from the main checkout's), compare commit ids exactly, read each candidate worktree's `HEAD` with `git -C {worktree} rev-parse HEAD`, resolve paths through `canonicalRealpath`, and fail closed on every inconclusive read.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — E1 tail loop in `runInner`: the `MERGE_HEAD` live-query exemption and `wd-merge-finish` event
- `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` — step 5 Resolve-now bullet: drop the E1 chase
- `docs/hooks.md` — E1 posture bullets
- `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` — allow and fail-closed cases
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `appendEvent` (no change expected)

## Gotchas

- The exemption must sit after the `otherWorktrees` check and before the `foreign`-ownership branch. That way it never reclassifies a commit already allowed as `wd-ambiguous`, and a `foreign` caller keeps its existing allow + `systemMessage`.
- Under `worktree-always`, the fast-forward of the main checkout is `git merge --ff-only`, which is not a `commit` target, so only the scratch-worktree commit needs the exemption. Confirm with `gitTargetsFrom` before assuming otherwise.
- An octopus merge lists several commits in `MERGE_HEAD`; require every line to match, so a merge that also pulls in an unrelated branch keeps today's deny.
- The `worktree-merge.md` bullet is pinned by #3809's conformance tests; keep "this branch's run is closed first" and the step 4 re-protection wording intact.

## Original request

Let E1 allow a multi-run reconciliation's conflict-resolution commit without closing sibling runs

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3809

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's **Resolve now** bullet carries a multi-run chase: the conflict resolution ends in a commit in the main checkout, which the working-directory hook (E1, `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) checks against the newest non-terminal run in the project regardless of owner (`plugin/bin/hooks.js` resolveRunDir, owner-unfiltered). So before the commit can land, the procedure closes this branch's run, then every other reconciliation branch's run E1 names in turn, and must re-protect each one when the resolution lands or is abandoned.

That one bullet drew #3809's whole-branch review Important 1, part of fix round 1, and four /review findings (3c at :126 reproduced, plus single-agent 3b :126, 3c :139, 3f :138). The prose workaround is correct now but is the most fragile part of the procedure, and it exists only because E1 cannot tell that a main-checkout commit belongs to a human-present reconciliation.

## Deliverables

Decide how E1 should treat a commit in the main checkout made while reconciling several runs' branches — so the reconciliation does not have to close sibling runs to get its resolution commit through — and implement that decision in the hook.

Then simplify `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's Resolve-now bullet to drop the E1 chase, keeping the per-branch close-run ordering #3809 pinned.

## Open Question

Which signal should let E1 allow this commit without closing other runs: a run-state marker that the reconciliation sets (and clears) on each run it is merging, a reconciliation-scoped exemption keyed on MERGE_HEAD naming a branch whose run is in the reconciliation, or narrowing E1's owner-unfiltered newest-run resolution for the main checkout? Each changes the never-break-a-session posture in docs/hooks.md differently.

## Release Note

Resolving a merge conflict during a multi-run local-merge reconciliation no longer has to close other branches' runs first.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — E1 decision for a reconciliation commit in the main checkout
- `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` — drop step 5's E1 chase

groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: ledger resolve gate (#3304 final review, I3)
**Related:** #3304, #3675, #3818, #3820, #3876, #3936

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/harness-refusal.js` defines `REFUSAL_FRAGMENTS` (`This session`, ` is isolated in the worktree `, `Refusing to run it`) and `HARNESS_ISOLATION_REFUSAL_RE`, which require the noun `This session`. `post-tool-use-failure.js` uses the regex to log a `wd-guard-refusal` event, and `bash-prefilter.js` uses the signature. The reflect Friction lens reads those events. `tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml`'s `claude-code` entry asserts each fragment against the installed binary, and `tests/harness-refusal-drift-pin.test.js` keeps the two in lockstep.

Probed against the installed Claude Code 2.1.302 binary (2026-10-24), the refusal noun is chosen by one function:

```
function NI(e){return Tl()?.worktreePath===e
  ? {noun:"This session",possessive:"a worktree-isolated session's"}
  : {noun:"This agent",possessive:"a worktree-isolated agent's"}}
```

So every refusal template (`${noun} is isolated in the worktree …`) says `This agent` whenever the worktree is not the session's own, which is the case for a subagent dispatched with its own isolation worktree. Two more templates are fixed strings: `This agent is isolated in the worktree … no longer exists and the only recovery target is the parent session's shared checkout. Refusing to run there …` and a `${noun}` variant ending `Refusing to run there. Report this instead of retrying.` Neither the `This agent` noun nor `Refusing to run there` matches today's regex, so those refusals produce no `wd-guard-refusal` event.

Lens agents running inside the parent session's own worktree do say `This session` and were counted. That is how #3480's roughly 14 lens-agent refusals surfaced and led to #3675's dispatch-prompt fix. The same waste from an agent in its own isolation worktree is invisible today.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Count both: widen the matcher to the `This agent` noun and to the worktree-gone `Refusing to run there` ending, keeping the `This session` match unchanged
- [ ] Add two fields to each `wd-guard-refusal` event: `actor` (`session` or `agent`, read from the noun) and `variant` (`guard` for the command-shape and different-worktree refusals, `worktree-gone` for the two "no longer exists" templates), so the Friction lens can report the operator's own friction separately from dispatched agents' and flag lost isolation
- [ ] Update `REFUSAL_FRAGMENTS` and the `claude-code` manifest `must-match` values together (noun alternatives plus the `Refusing to run there` signature), and keep `tests/harness-refusal-drift-pin.test.js` in lockstep
- [ ] Have the reflect Friction lens break the count down by `actor` and call out any `worktree-gone` event by name

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/hooks-harness-refusal.test.js` logs a `wd-guard-refusal` event for each of: a `This session … Refusing to run it` refusal (`actor: session`), a `This agent … Refusing to run it` refusal (`actor: agent`), a `This agent … Refusing to run it there` different-worktree refusal, and both worktree-gone templates (`variant: worktree-gone`); and logs none for an unrelated Bash failure
- Reverting the widened regex turns the agent and worktree-gone cases red, while the session case stays green
- `tools/upstream-drift`'s `claude-code` check passes against 2.1.302 with the new `must-match` values, and the drift-pin test passes
- `bash-prefilter.js`'s signature check still fires on every matched refusal
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Reflect's friction report now counts worktree-guard refusals hit by dispatched agents, not just by the main session.

## Technical Approach

The question was whether these refusals are the run operator's friction. They are the run's friction either way. A dispatched agent's refused command is a wasted turn the run pays for, and it is almost always caused by the dispatch prompt the run wrote, which is exactly the signal that produced #3675's fix. Leaving the narrow match would keep that signal for agents sharing the parent's worktree but hide it for agents in their own, an accident of how the agent was dispatched rather than a deliberate scope. The `actor` field keeps "my own friction" answerable without discarding the rest.

Build the regex from fragments as today: a noun alternation (`This session|This agent`), the isolation clause, a lazy gap, then `Refusing to run` followed by ` it` or ` there`. Derive `actor` from the matched noun, and `variant` from the presence of "no longer exists".

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/harness-refusal.js` — fragments, nouns, signature, regex
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use-failure.js` — event fields `actor` / `variant`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/bash-prefilter.js` — signature check derived from the module
- `tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml` — `claude-code` `must-match` values and their comment block
- `tests/hooks-harness-refusal.test.js` — new matcher cases
- `tests/harness-refusal-drift-pin.test.js` — lockstep pin
- `plugin/skills/reflect/full-mode.md` — the Friction lens's breakdown by `actor` (the file that reads `wd-guard-refusal`)

## Gotchas

- `harness-refusal.js` must still require nothing (`bash-prefilter.js` loads it on every failed Bash call), so build the widened regex from string constants only.
- The manifest's comment records per-version occurrence counts (`noun:"This session"` 1x at 2.1.302, and so on); update the counts with the new fragments, measured against the installed binary, not guessed.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: a subagent's failed Bash call fires the parent session's `PostToolUseFailure` hook with the refusal text intact (the #3480 lens-agent events suggest yes for agents in the parent's worktree); confirm the same for an agent dispatched with `isolation: "worktree"` before relying on the new `actor: agent` events appearing.

## Original request

Decide whether friction events should count the subagent and worktree-gone isolation refusals

Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

`HARNESS_ISOLATION_REFUSAL_RE` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/harness-refusal.js` matches only the session noun ("This session is isolated in the worktree ... Refusing to run it"). A subagent's refusal ("This agent is isolated in the worktree ...") and the worktree-gone variant (ending "Refusing to run there") are not logged as `wd-guard-refusal`, so the reflect Friction lens never sees them. Found in #3304's final review (I3).

## Deliverables

Make the decision, then either widen `HARNESS_ISOLATION_REFUSAL_RE` and `REFUSAL_FRAGMENTS` (with the manifest must-match values and the pin tests) or record that the narrow match is intended.

## Open Question

Should the Friction lens count a subagent's and a worktree-gone refusal as the run operator's friction? If yes, widen the regex and `REFUSAL_FRAGMENTS` together with the manifest `claude-code` must-match values; if no, record that the narrow match is intended.

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/harness-refusal.js` — fragments and regex
- `tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml` — claude-code assertions

groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: SDD whole-branch review of #3595 (run 2026-10-20T124821-spec-3599-3602-3695-3696-3698-3699-3595), finding 2
**Related:** #3812, #3942, #2713, #3396, #3467, #3646, #3721, #3744, #3754, #3843, #3847, #3877, #3878, #3900, #3901, #3902, #3903, #3904, #3968, #3976

## Current State

Under `integration-model: pr-first`, wrap-up's branch-finish merge runs at `review-console.md`'s "On approval" step 13 (#3595): after the console's step-12 commit and a push, before step 14 hands off to Phase 4's execution step (`execution-and-verification.md`). Everything the execution step changes in the tree therefore lands after `gh pr merge`, on a branch that is already merged, and its "Phase exit" push targets that merged branch. Nothing checks that a commit made after the merge is empty (`_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 1.5 guards only curation-engine commits).

Inventory of the execution step's actions on `origin/main`, classified against the console's steps 1-13 (`review-console.md`, `review-console-appendix.md`'s Resolution-to-step mapping, `cleanup-procedures.md`'s canonical list):

| Action | Changes tracked files? | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| Reference repairs (staged, approved) | yes | **post-merge residue** — the mapping says a Reference repairs row "has no numbered step of its own — it is applied by Phase 4's execution step" |
| Genre convention resolution | yes — `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` write, plus `git mv` and reference rewrites on migration | **post-merge residue** — no console step applies it |
| Cleanup item 3 (design caches) | yes — deletes `docs/plans/*-audit.json`/`-recommendations.json`/`-declined.json` (not gitignored) | **post-merge residue** |
| Cleanup item 1 (plans) | yes, under `superpowers-plans-retention: prune-after-wrapup`, and for any leftover `*-design.md` | **post-merge residue** (conditional) |
| Cleanup item 5 (record lifecycle) | yes under `work-backend: local-files` (`closeRecord` + commit); no-op under `github-issues` | **post-merge residue** (conditional) |
| Execution step's own commit + phase-exit push | carries all of the above | **post-merge residue** |
| Documentation, CLAUDE.md/rules, ADRs, new docs (D2), skill updates | yes | **already applied** by console steps 2-5; the execution step's apply list re-lists them |
| Docs-health restructural filings (D1) | no (GitHub issues) | **already applied** by console step 3 — a second pass risks a duplicate `gh issue create` |
| Memory, upstream feedback | no | already confirm-only |
| Acceptance labeling | no (labels, comments) | not tree-changing |
| Cleanup items 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 | no / already routed | item 2 already runs at step 13; item 4's merge is step 13; 6/7 are not tree changes; item 8's run dir is gitignored |

Under "Approve all, leave PR open" no merge runs, so the execution step's commit and push are correct there today — only the merge path is wrong.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Make `pr-first`'s branch finish run once, **after the last tree-changing action of the wrap-up** and before cleanup item 4's worktree removal, instead of at console step 13. Every residue row in the table then reaches the PR head before `gh pr merge`, and the execution step's commit and phase-exit push target a live branch. Item 2's delete-ledger keeps its "after the ledger's last writers, before the merge" placement.
- [ ] The finish still runs when the execution step is skipped ("No actions to execute") and when the console is skipped (empty-console fast path) — one finish point reached on every path, never zero or two
- [ ] Under `pr-first`, the execution step's apply-list entries that console steps 2-5 already applied (Documentation, CLAUDE.md/rules, ADRs, new docs, skill updates, docs-health filings) become confirm-only, the way Memory and Upstream feedback already are — no second application and no second `gh issue create`
- [ ] Update every citation of "step 13" as the merge point: `cleanup-procedures.md`'s Item 2 paragraph, `cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section C, `merge-mode.md` step 1, and the `auto-merge-short-circuit.md` / `flow/multispec-review-console.md` ordering notes that cite it
- [ ] `local-merge` and `current-branch` behavior is unchanged

## Acceptance Criteria

- A conformance test pins that, under `pr-first`, no tree-changing action in `execution-and-verification.md` or cleanup items 1, 3, and 5 is ordered after the branch-finish merge; reverting the reorder turns it red
- The same test (or a sibling) pins that the execution step's apply list marks the console-applied entries confirm-only under `pr-first`
- A `pr-first` "Approve all + merge" run with a design-wrapper cache or an approved reference repair produces a squash commit containing that change, and no commit lands on the branch after the merge — checked against a real run before and after the fix, quoting the PR's commit list
- "Approve all, leave PR open" still pushes the execution step's commit to the open PR
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Wrap-up's final cleanup and commit now land in the merged PR instead of on an already-merged branch.

## Technical Approach

The root cause is the merge's position, not any one action, so the fix moves the merge rather than chasing each residue item into the console. Adding console steps for reference repairs, genre conventions, and cleanup items 1/3/5 would fix today's inventory, but every future execution-step action would reopen the gap. With one finish point after the last tree writer, new actions are covered by default.

Suggested shape (the builder may choose another that meets the constraints): console steps 1-12 unchanged; step 13 becomes "item 2 + push" only (or folds into the execution step); the execution step runs its tree-changing work, commits, and pushes; then a single Branch finish step runs `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` (or leave-open), then cleanup items 4, 6, 7, 8. When the execution step is skipped, the Branch finish step still runs straight after the console.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — "On approval" steps 13-14
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — apply list (confirm-only under `pr-first`), commit, phase-exit push, leave-open re-check

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build` runs its `plan-authoring-checks.md` checks against a plan, but none of them asks whether a project skill already governs a file the plan touches. Dispatched SDD implementers and reviewers see only their task brief, so a rule that lives only in a `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` never reaches them unless the plan quotes it.

The plan's Global Constraints defined "provably owned" as `isTrustedOwnedRun` plus not ad-hoc, which is weaker than `pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions`' existing rule that a deny keyed on the caller's own run must also require `classifyOwnership === 'mine'`. - [ ] Pin the new check with a conformance test, following the file's existing pinned checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` carries a check that names `.claude/skills/` and requires governing project-skill rules to be quoted into the plan's Global Constraints.
2. A test under `tests/` fails when that check's paragraph is removed from `plan-authoring-checks.md`.

Build plans now carry any project-skill rule that governs the files they touch, so subagents implementing a task see it.

Surface: infra

Origin: reflect (light mode, Friction lens) from #3675's wrap-up run (2026-10-20T162315-record-3675).
**Related:** #3690 (absorbed), #3188, #3295, #3737, #3740, #3812, #3898, #3956, #3963

## Current State

In #3675's dispatch group, both dispatched Task calls — `build,test` and `review,polish,wrap-up` — found mid-run that no `Agent`/`Task` tool was available, ran their work inline, and each self-reported the gap in `decisions.md` as a `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` deviation. Nothing defective shipped, but the same discovery happened twice in one run.

Since then, half of this is settled. #3078 (`364762254`) gave `_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Foreground Execution Discipline a **Fallback** for "no `Agent`/`Task` tool exists (`ToolSearch` finds none, deferred or otherwise — the normal case in a cloud routine sandbox)", restated in `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s Context pack item 7: judge the unit in-session, log the downgrade, mark its findings `unconfirmed`. That covers read-only units (lenses, single reads, judges) — the review call's side.

The build side is still uncovered, and two rules now contradict each other there:

- The Fallback is explicitly limited to read-only units; for a write-capable child it says only that one still silent at the bound is never redone in-session (because an abandoned child keeps running and may still write).
- `build/execution-mode-policy.md` (#491) rules that executing the plan's substance directly in-session, skipping Task dispatch, is **never licensed** — under a locked `execution-strategy: subagent-only` or otherwise.

The same environment has already produced two different outcomes. In run `2026-10-20T022848-record-3630` (record #3630, filed as #3690, absorbed here), the dispatched build stopped at `/build`'s Common Step 2 before any implementation (#3690's report calls it a HARD-GATE; `build/SKILL.md` has no gate by that literal name there, so the stop presumably came from the call honoring `execution-mode-policy.md`'s never-licensed rule), and Settle classified it `transient` and kept `auto:build`, so every retry in that sandbox would stop the same way. In #3675's run, the build ran inline instead and reported a concern.

So a dispatched `build,test` call under `execution-strategy: subagent-only` that has no `Agent` tool has no compliant path: `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development` cannot dispatch implementers, inline execution is forbidden, and nothing says to stop. #3675's call improvised inline execution and reported it as a concern. Nothing about this case is anomalous — the core file itself calls it the normal case in a cloud routine sandbox — yet each call discovers it mid-run, after the plan is written.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Foreground Execution Discipline names the **no-nested-agent environment** once, as an expected environment class, and distinguishes its two cases: a child abandoned at the bound (today's rule — a write-capable one is never redone in-session) versus a child that was **never launched because no `Agent` tool exists** (no child exists, so nothing can still be writing, and the unit — write-capable or not — is done in-session)
- [ ] `build/execution-mode-policy.md` gains one carve-out to #491's "never licensed": a dispatched Task call (not the interactive orchestrating session) that has no `Agent` tool executes the plan in-session. State why this keeps #491's rationale: the dispatched call is already a clean room separate from the session that dispatched it, and the second Task call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) remains a separate agent, so the review is still independent of the code's author
- [ ] `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first-call (`build,test`) template tells the call to probe for the `Agent` tool once, **before** choosing an execution strategy (one `ToolSearch`), and on no tool to take the carve-out from the start instead of discovering it mid-plan; Context pack item 7 carries the same distinction for any dispatch that writes
- [ ] The downgrade logs as one canonical `decisions.md` `AUTO` entry (per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s schema) naming the environment — e.g. `no nested Agent tool — plan executed in-session` — and the call returns `STATUS: DONE`, not `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`, when that was the only deviation
- [ ] The read-only Fallback keeps its `unconfirmed` marking unchanged — a self-judged lens finding is still weaker evidence than a second reader's

## Acceptance Criteria

- `subagent-dispatch-core.md` states that a write-capable unit whose child was never launched (no `Agent` tool) is executed in-session, and that a write-capable child abandoned at the bound still ends `STATUS: BLOCKED` — both rules present, and distinguishable by whether a child was ever launched
- `build/execution-mode-policy.md` names the dispatched-call-with-no-`Agent`-tool carve-out and still states that the interactive orchestrating session may never execute the plan directly
- `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s `build,test` template contains the up-front probe instruction, ordered before the execution-strategy choice
- `tests/foreground-execution-instruction.test.js` (or the suite that pins these sections) asserts the new never-launched-vs-abandoned distinction in the core section, item 7, and the build template, and reverting the core-file sentence turns it red
- The canonical `AUTO` line's wording is pinned in one place and cited, not restated, by the template
- A `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` firing against a `subagent-only` record, in an environment whose dispatched Task call has no `Agent` tool, builds via the carve-out rather than stopping at Common Step 2 or being settled `transient` (the #3690 failure)
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Dispatched builds in sandboxes without nested agents now follow a defined path instead of improvising and flagging a concern.

## Technical Approach

The key distinction is whether a child was ever launched. The existing "never redo a write-capable child in-session" rule exists because an abandoned child keeps running and may still write (`subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Fallback). With no `Agent` tool there is no child, so that hazard cannot occur, and in-session execution of a write-capable unit is safe. Write that reasoning into the core file once, and have `task-prompt.md` item 7 and the `build,test` template restate the rule (they are inlined verbatim into a `Task()` prompt whose agent never reads the core file — `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `subagent-dispatch-core.md` row).

The probe is one `ToolSearch` for the `Agent` tool at the start of the `build,test` call. A probe by the top-level dispatcher would not work: the dispatcher has a Task tool by construction (it is dispatching), and whether its children get a nested one depends on the environment and Claude Code version (`subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Background-work paragraph, #3722's measurements).

#491's carve-out is narrow on purpose: it licenses in-session execution only for a dispatched Task call that has no `Agent` tool. An interactive session that has the tool and chooses not to use it is still non-compliant.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md` — Foreground Execution Discipline: name the environment class; never-launched vs abandoned
- `plugin/skills/build/execution-mode-policy.md` — the dispatched-call carve-out to #491
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — Context pack item 7 and the `build,test` template's up-front probe
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md` — only if the canonical entry needs a new reason slug
- `tests/foreground-execution-instruction.test.js` — pins the core section, item 7, and both templates
- `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — check for pinned Fallback wording
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — the `subagent-dispatch-core.md` edge row describing what item 7 restates

## Gotchas

- `/flow`'s `multispec-parallel-waves.md` inlines item 7 and the `build,test` clause verbatim (`docs/skill-graph.md`), so changing either changes what parallel-wave members receive — update that file in the same change.
- `tests/foreground-execution-instruction.test.js` pins the core section, item 7, and both templates against each other; edit all four together or it goes red.
- The decision is about the dispatched Task call, not `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development` itself (an upstream skill this repo does not edit) — the carve-out tells the call to execute the plan in-session in place of invoking that skill.
- #3188 (open) proposes mechanical enforcement of `execution-strategy: subagent-only` (a PreToolUse check or a `/build` Step 2 assertion). Whatever it lands must honor this carve-out — a dispatched call with no `Agent` tool executing in-session is compliant, not a violation.
- `/build`'s Common Step 2 is where #3630's build stopped; the carve-out has to be reachable from there (the probe result decides the execution strategy before Common Step 2 resolves it), or the build stops anyway.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: #3675's two calls lacked the tool because of the environment (cloud sandbox or a headless Claude Code version), not a one-off harness fault — the run's `decisions.md` was not preserved in the archive, so confirm the class by checking `subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Background-work measurements against the run's environment if it can be identified.

## Original request

Dispatch contract doesn't name or detect an Agent/Task-tool-less sandbox

Origin: reflect (light mode, Friction lens) from #3675's wrap-up run (2026-10-20T162315-record-3675).
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s subagent contract, and `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`'s
two-call gate, assume `execution-strategy: subagent-only` dispatched Task calls have the
Agent/Task tool available for nested fan-out. In this run's dispatch group (record #3675), both
dispatched calls — `build,test` and `review,polish,wrap-up` — independently discovered mid-run
that no Agent/Task tool was available, and both fell back to running their work inline, each
self-reporting the gap in `decisions.md` as a `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` deviation. Both degraded
gracefully and no defect landed in the shipped work, but the gap recurred identically across two
independent calls in the same run rather than being a one-off anomaly.

## Open Question

Should the dispatch contract (or dispatch's own two-call gate) detect Agent/Task-tool absence up
front — either declaring the limitation inline in the dispatch prompt's own preamble, or treating
a Task-tool-less sandbox as a named, expected environment class — rather than leaving each
dispatched call to discover and self-report the gap independently every time? Or is the existing
per-call self-report-and-degrade pattern (DONE_WITH_CONCERNS + a decisions.md note) sufficient as
is, given it already surfaces the gap without blocking?

## Release Note

n/a — no code change proposed yet; this issue exists to get a maintainer decision on whether one
is warranted.

Surface: infra

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3664, ledger rows 3-4)
**Related:** #3664, #3646, #3792, #3942

## Current State

The ephemeral dev server a pipeline starts (`_shared/dev-url-detection.md`'s Ephemeral server start, items 3-4) is recorded as one line, `{pid} {port} {worktree-root} detached:{yes|no}`, in `ephemeral-server.txt`. POSIX launches under `setsid` and records `detached:yes`; Windows has no detach primitive and records `detached:no` (`dev-url-detection.md:130-131`). The recorded pid is the shell leader; the listening socket can belong to its child.

Every stop identifies the server only by that pid and port. `wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section D (#3664) validates the record's shape and keeps it when the port is still held after the kill, but proves neither identity:

- **Kill side (step 2):** any positive-integer pid is signalled (`kill {pid}`, plus `kill -- -{pid}` under `detached:yes`; `taskkill /PID {pid} /T /F` on win32). A pid reused by an unrelated process after the server died gets killed, along with its tree on win32.
- **Port side (step 4):** a port still held after an "already stopped" pid is reported as the server's survivor, though the holder may be an unrelated process.

A "pid listens on port" probe does not settle it, because the listener is usually the leader's child, and after the leader dies a non-detached child is reparented, so a parent-chain walk breaks.

The same stop logic is restated as agent-read prose in other places: `review/step3-routing.md`'s fix-wave server coordination (around line 124), `_shared/dev-url-detection.md`'s standalone stop, `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s shared teardown (line 176), and `flow/multispec-parallel-waves.md`'s per-member stop (line 54). Each guard is pinned by text, not by behavior.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Identity rule:** a process is identified by `(pid, start time)`. When the server starts, capture two identities: the **leader** (the pid recorded today) and the **listener** (the process holding the port once the readiness poll in item 3 succeeds). Write both, with start times, to a sidecar `ephemeral-server.json` beside `ephemeral-server.txt`. The txt line keeps its format, since `detached:` is parsed as its last token.
- [ ] **Kill side:** signal a recorded process only when its current start time matches the recorded one; a mismatch or a missing pid is "already stopped". Under `detached:yes`, the group kill stays keyed on the verified leader.
- [ ] **Port side:** after the kill, a port holder is the server's survivor only when it matches the recorded listener identity, or (under `detached:yes`) its process group is the recorded leader's. Any other holder is reported as "port {port} held by unrelated pid {x}", and the record is deleted, since the recorded server is gone.
- [ ] **One executable helper:** add a `plugin/bin/` CLI (e.g. `dev-server.js` with `record` and `stop` verbs, using the injectable-runner seam in `.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI wrapper contract). Every prose site above calls it instead of restating the stop: the Ephemeral server start's item 4 (record), Section D, `step3-routing.md`, the standalone stop, and both `/flow` multi-spec teardown sites (stop).
- [ ] **Legacy records:** a run whose record has no sidecar (started before this change) keeps today's behavior, logged once as `identity unverified (legacy record)`. Give that branch a removal condition per this repo's deprecation rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests with a fake process table: a recorded pid whose start time differs is not signalled and reports already stopped; a matching one is signalled; a port held by the recorded listener (alive after a leader-only stop) is reported as the survivor and the record is kept; a port held by an unrelated process is reported as unrelated and the record is deleted; a `detached:yes` child in the leader's process group counts as the survivor
- Each of those tests goes red against a helper that skips the identity check
- A conformance test asserts that none of the stop sites restate `kill {pid}` / `taskkill /PID` / an `lsof … | xargs kill` stop inline and that each one calls the helper
- A live probe on macOS (and Linux in CI where available) starts a real `setsid` shell-leader server, records it, and stops it through the helper, with the leader and listener identities matching what `ps` reports
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Pipeline cleanup no longer signals a process that merely reused a dead dev server's pid, and no longer blames an unrelated process for a port it failed to free.

## Technical Approach

The two candidate rules in the original question were a pid-listens-on-port probe (it fails for the shell-leader/child shape, as the record notes) and some stronger identity. Start time is the standard way to tell a reused pid from the original. POSIX: `ps -o lstart= -p {pid}` or `ps -o etimes=`; win32: `Win32_Process.CreationDate` via PowerShell `Get-CimInstance`. A reused pid cannot share its predecessor's start time. Capturing the listener's own identity at start, instead of deriving it from the leader at stop, sidesteps the reparenting problem entirely.

Listener lookup at record time: POSIX `lsof -nP -iTCP:{port} -sTCP:LISTEN -t`, with `ss -ltnp` as a fallback where `lsof` is absent; win32 `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort {port} -State Listen` → `OwningProcess`.

Fail direction: an identity the helper cannot read (no `ps`, a CIM failure) is unprovable, so it signals nothing and reports a cleanup failure, keeping the record. A leaked dev server is recoverable; a killed unrelated process is not.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/dev-server.js` — new CLI: `record` and `stop` verbs
- `plugin/bin/lib/dev-server/` — new module: identity capture, verify, stop (injectable runner)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — Ephemeral server start item 4 (record via helper), standalone stop
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — Section D steps 2-4 call the helper

- `tests/bin-lib/dev-server/` — unit tests with a fake process table
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI and module

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `ps -o lstart=` and `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` return a start time stable enough to compare exactly (second resolution) on the CI runners; if `etimes` is used instead, compare with a small tolerance and test the boundary.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: once the readiness poll succeeds, the listener is already bound and visible to `lsof`/`ss`/`Get-NetTCPConnection` without elevated privileges on macOS, Linux CI, and win32 CI. The original record noted no probe had been run against a real `detached:no` / `detached:yes` leader — run one before relying on it.
- The `bin/` CLIs must not read `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` at runtime (unset in Bash); follow the existing CLIs' process-cwd anchoring.
- `multispec-parallel-waves.md`'s members may start servers without a run-dir sidecar path; check where each member writes its record before wiring the helper.

## Original request

wrap-up Section D never proves the recorded pid or port belongs to the server it recorded

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3664, ledger rows 3-4)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

wrap-up Section D (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md`) identifies the dev server it stops only by the pid and port in `ephemeral-server.txt`. #3664 made it validate the record's shape (four fields, positive-integer pid and port, a `detached:` token) and keep the record when the port is still held after the kill, but nothing proves the recorded pid is still the server it was recorded for. Kill side: step 2 signals any positive-integer pid, so a pid reused by an unrelated process after the server died is signalled. Port side: step 4 reports a port still held after an "already stopped" pid as the survivor, though the holder may be an unrelated process. A pid-listens-on-port probe does not settle it: a `detached:no` or `detached:yes` record names the shell leader, and the listening socket belongs to its child. The stop logic is also agent-read prose in three places (Section D, review's fix-wave server coordination in `step3-routing.md`, and the standalone stop in `_shared/dev-url-detection.md`), so each guard is pinned by text, not by behavior. Refs #3664 (its review ledger rows 3-4).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide the identity rule: how the recorded server is told from an unrelated process on the recorded pid (kill side) and on the recorded port (port side), covering the shell-leader and child-socket record shapes on POSIX and win32.
- [ ] Apply the rule in every place that stops a recorded dev server, preferably through one executable stop helper the three prose sites call, so the rule is tested by behavior.
- [ ] Pin it with a test that fails against the current text.

## Open Question

Which identity check is sound for the shell-leader and child-socket shapes `ephemeral-server.txt` legitimately records, and is a single executable stop helper the right home for it? Insufficient evidence: no probe has been tried against a real `detached:no` / `detached:yes` leader.

## Release Note

Pipeline cleanup no longer signals a process that merely reused a dead dev server's pid, and no longer blames an unrelated process for a port it failed to free.

## Technical Approach

groups.body:
Surface: terminal

## Current State

`hooks.js archive-run --run <dir>` calls `archiveRunDir` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`). When the run's `work/` is git-tracked, that function `git mv`s it into `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/` and commits on the main checkout's current branch (`archive-merged.js:1302`, `[reconcile] archive run {runId}`, scoped to its own paths per #2241). The function returns only `{ ok: true, movedEntries }` (`archive-merged.js:1503`), so the CLI (`plugin/bin/hooks.js:1249-1252`) prints the `moved: …` lines and `claude-tweaks: archived {run-id}`. Nothing tells the caller that a commit landed, on which branch, or that it is unpushed.

Observed twice:
- In a consuming project (the original request below): the silent commit left local `master` ahead of origin, and a deploy script hard-stops on that.
- In this repo on 2026-10-21: a `/claude-tweaks:sweep` run archived 69 run dirs via `archive-run`. Four of them carried tracked `work/` and produced four unreported `[reconcile] archive run` commits on local `main` (`d48c523e0`, `6cf4efb34`, `325facfe8`, `d447003fe`). They were only noticed through a manual `git log`.

#3396 tracks the broader mechanism (unpushed reconcile archive commits on the main checkout). This record is the output gap only, which is separately fixable.

## Deliverables

1. `archiveRunDir` reports the commit it made: on success with a commit, its return value carries `commit: { sha, branch }` (short sha of the `[reconcile] archive run` commit, plus the checked-out branch name). `commit` is absent when no tracked content moved and no commit ran.
2. `hooks.js archive-run` prints one line after `archived {run-id}` whenever `commit` is present: `claude-tweaks: committed {sha} on {branch} (not pushed — {n} ahead of {upstream})`. When the branch has no upstream, the parenthetical reads `(no upstream configured)`. When the ahead-count probe fails, it reads `(push state unknown)`. The line never fails the verb.
3. The reconcile archival path that calls `archiveRunDir` surfaces the same `commit` field in its per-run result entry, so `hooks.js reconcile --json` consumers see it too.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Archiving a fixture run with tracked `work/` returns `commit.sha` matching `git rev-parse --short HEAD` after the call, and `commit.branch` matching the checked-out branch. Archiving a fixture with no tracked content returns no `commit` field.
2. `archive-run` stdout on a tracked-work fixture contains a line matching `/^claude-tweaks: committed [0-9a-f]{7,} on \S+ \((not pushed — \d+ ahead of \S+|no upstream configured|push state unknown)\)$/m`. On an untracked-only fixture, stdout contains no `committed` line.
3. The ahead count is correct: a fixture whose branch tracks an upstream at the pre-archive commit reports `1 ahead`.
4. The reconcile `--json` run entry for an archived tracked-work run includes the `commit` object.
5. Existing `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` cases still pass unchanged, including the `moved:`-line cases.

## Release Note

archive-run now tells you when it commits the archive move, on which branch, and whether that commit is still unpushed.

## Technical Approach

Capture the commit's sha right after the successful `commitGit` call in `archiveRunDir`, using `git rev-parse --short HEAD` plus `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD` through the same `runGit` seam, and thread it into the success return. In `hooks.js`, compute the ahead count with `git rev-list --count @{upstream}..HEAD` (anchored `-C mainRoot`), degrading to the two fallback parentheticals. Reconcile's archive call site copies the field into its result entry. Pushing, or skipping the commit on the integration branch (the request's optional alternatives), is out of scope. Those are behavior changes that belong to #3396's mechanism decision.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveRunDir` returns `commit: { sha, branch }` after a successful commit; the reconcile call site (around line 1870) carries it into the run entry
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `archive-run` prints the committed/ahead line
- `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` — new stdout assertions for the committed line
- `tests/reconcile.test.js` — `archiveRunDir` return-shape assertion for `commit`

## Gotchas

- `archive-run`'s stdout is documented as informational human text that no caller parses (`hooks.js` comment above `archiveRunDir`), so adding a line is not a contract change. The `--json` run-entry field is additive.
- Resolve the ahead count from `mainRoot`, not from `process.cwd()`. A worktree cwd has a different HEAD (`[IL-127]`-style shadowing).
- An unborn or detached HEAD has no symbolic ref. Report the branch as `detached` rather than throwing.

## Original request

archive-run: commits the archive move on the current branch without reporting the commit or that it is unpushed

**Summary:** `hooks.js archive-run` commits the archive move on the main checkout's current branch, but its output never mentions the commit or that it is unpushed.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/hooks.js archive-run` → `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` (around line 1169)

**Use case:**
After `close-run`, `hooks.js archive-run --run <dir>` was run in the main checkout, which was on the integration branch (`master`). It `git mv`'d the run's `work/*-spec.md` files into `pipelines/archive/` and committed them as `[reconcile] archive run <run-id>`. The commit is correctly scoped to its own paths (#2241). The CLI output listed only `moved: …` lines and `archived <run-id>`. It never said that a commit was made, on which branch, or that the commit was not pushed.

In this project, local `master` being ahead of `origin/master` is a hard stop for the deploy script, which refuses to run until the commit is pushed. The remote host's nightly backup also commits and pushes without pulling, so a push made later, but not deployed, can leave that backup's push rejected. The commit was only noticed by chance (`git worktree list` showed `master` at a new SHA), and it took a push plus a deploy to clear.

Repro:
1. Main checkout on the integration branch, in sync with origin.
2. `hooks.js close-run --run <run-dir>`, then `hooks.js archive-run --run <run-dir>` for a run whose `work/` holds tracked spec files.
3. `git status -sb` now shows `ahead 1`, but nothing in the archive-run output said so.

Suggested change: have `archive-run` (and the reconcile pass that calls the same code) report the commit in its output, for example `committed <short-sha> on <branch> (not pushed — <n> ahead of <upstream>)`. Optionally, offer a `--push` flag, or skip the commit when the checked-out branch is the integration branch and leave the moves staged with a note. At minimum, say that the commit exists.

Related: #3396 tracks the same symptom in this repo: unpushed `[reconcile] archive run` commits on the main checkout's local `main`. Its Deliverable 2 asks which mechanism leaves them there. This report is that mechanism seen from a consuming project, plus the output gap, which is fixable separately.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.145.0

Surface: infra

Origin: windows-regression.yml post-merge check on 3ad36593f (PR #4335, #4133)

## Current State

The post-merge Windows check on 3ad36593f (run 40288495705, base 9aaf50f45) attributes two new failures in `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js`: "AC1.1: a require records its candidates up to the one it resolves to, minus those under an earlier probe" and "AC1.1: a require resolves the way Node does — paths option, package.json main, bare node_modules lookups". #4133 added both tests in that commit. Both fail with `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaksclaude-tweakstoolstest-impacttracer.js'`.

That error is the NODE_OPTIONS backslash class. At 3ad36593f the test's `traceEnv` built `` `--require "${TRACER}"` `` from a native path (`tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js:39` at 9aaf50f45). Node's NODE_OPTIONS parser treats `\` inside double quotes as an escape, so on win32 the preload path loses its backslashes and the tracer never loads. Every traced test in the file failed the same way on Windows before 3ad36593f, as #4134's absorbed #4254 section records. Baseline adjudication counts only these two as new because they did not exist at the base.

**Probed at shaping time (2026-10-26) against `origin/main`: already fixed, not yet confirmed on Windows.** PR #4316 (#4134, merged 2026-10-26T10:51:30Z as 7e9b02af4, 4 commits after 3ad36593f) did three things:

- It added `tools/test-impact/node-options.js`'s `requireOption(p, pathImpl)`, which forward-slashes the path before quoting it.
- It switched `traceEnv` (`tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js:40` on main) and both fixture preloads (`:242`, `:311`) to it.
- It pinned the win32 branch in `tests/test-impact-cli.test.js:38` with `path.win32`.

The two failing tests are now at `:183` and `:203` on main and go through `traceEnv`, so the fix covers them. #4316's own Windows proof (runs 40210345387, 40212335250 on 2026-10-25) ran on a branch based before 3ad36593f, so it never executed these two tests. The post-merge Windows run on 7e9b02af4 (40310659583) was still in progress at shaping time.

## Deliverables

1. Confirm on Windows that the two tests pass at or after 7e9b02af4. Read the `verify-report.json` (`failingFiles`) and the isolated log for `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` from a completed `windows-regression.yml` run whose head contains 7e9b02af4: the post-merge run 40310659583 once it finishes, or a fresh `workflow_dispatch` on main. Do not rely on the run's overall `success`, which only means "no new failures against its base".
2. If both pass, close #4388 as fixed by #4316, citing the run and the log lines. No code change.
3. If either still fails, record the new error text. A failure other than `Cannot find module 'D:a…'` is a different defect: fix it here if it is a fixture or expectation issue confined to `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js`, following `windows-checkout-test-parity`. Otherwise file it as its own record and close this one against #4316.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A completed `windows-regression.yml` run whose head contains 7e9b02af4 is cited, and its per-file evidence for `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` (from `verify-report.json` `failingFiles` and the isolated log) shows neither "AC1.1: a require records its candidates…" nor "AC1.1: a require resolves the way Node does…" failing.
- #4388 is closed with a comment naming that run and #4316, or Deliverable 3's branch is taken with its outcome recorded on the issue.
- If Deliverable 3 changes a test, `node --test tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux, and a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch after the last change shows the file clean.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: confirms two Windows test failures were fixed by the test-impact Windows tracing change.

## Technical Approach

This is verification first, with no expected code change. `requireOption` already removes the root cause on main, and its win32 branch is pinned on every host by `tests/test-impact-cli.test.js:38`. A Linux run cannot show the NODE_OPTIONS parse, so the evidence must come from a Windows run. Per the platform-proof rule, prove a per-file criterion from `verify-report.json`'s `failingFiles` plus the isolated log, not from the run's conclusion.

### Key Files

- `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` — the two AC1.1 tests (`:183`, `:203` on main); `traceEnv` at `:40`
- `tools/test-impact/node-options.js` — reference only (`requireOption`, added by #4316)
- `tests/test-impact-cli.test.js` — reference only (the `requireOption` win32 pin at `:38`)

## Gotchas

- A local checkout behind `origin/main` still shows the old `` `--require "${TRACER}"` `` at `:39` and no `tools/test-impact/node-options.js`. Build from a fresh `origin/main`, never from a stale base, or the record will look unfixed.
- The post-merge run's `success` conclusion is not proof. It compares against a base that already failed this file, so lingering failures would read as pre-existing, not new. Read the per-file report.
- `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` hangs in a subagent session on macOS (a known test-run pitfall), so a local re-run belongs in the main session or CI.
- A reviewer may simply close this record as fixed by #4316 once Deliverable 1's evidence is in hand. That is the expected outcome.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #4334, #3900, #4299, #4281, #4289, #4388, #3788, #3982, #3995, #4243, #4287, #4294, #4301, #4328

Origin: windows-regression.yml post-merge check on 456134058 (PR #4334, #3900)

## Current State

The post-merge Windows check on 456134058 (run 40278523944, base 4f437c57b) attributes three new failures across two files.

**`tests/hooks-git-exec.test.js` (1 test) is out of scope for this record.** "runGitAsync: opts.env is the spawn environment, same as runGit (#3900)" fails on the forward-slash vs backslash spelling of `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`. #4299 (ready) covers it explicitly in its Deliverable 1, together with its `runGit` twin. This record does not touch `hooks-git-exec.test.js`.

**`tests/hooks-policy-exemption.test.js` (2 tests) is this record's scope.** On Windows:

- "#3900 AC1.1: git -C "<repo>" push origin --delete feature-x from a non-isolated checkout is allowed" (`tests/hooks-policy-exemption.test.js:188`) is denied by the worktree-always gate.
- "#3900 AC1.1: the -C target, not the cwd, is the repo …" (`:209`) is denied on its allowed half (`:213`).

The cause is the fixture, not the gate. Both tests splice the native temp path into the command inside double quotes (`git -C "${repo}" push …`, `:191`, `:213`), so on Windows the command reads `git -C "D:\a\_temp\…" push origin --delete feature-x`. `DELETE_ONLY_PUSH_ALLOWLIST` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js:382`) admits the `-C` path through `CQ_ARG`. `CQ_ARG`'s double-quoted form, `CQ_DOUBLE` (`:324`), is a character class that excludes the double quote, `$`, the backtick and the backslash, with the comment "no $, backtick, or backslash inside". The #3900 grammar comment above the allowlist (`:370-373`) states the same exclusion on purpose. A backslashed Windows path in double quotes therefore never matches, the delete-only exemption never fires, and the push falls through to the deny. On macOS/Linux the temp path has no backslash, so the tests pass there.

Two sibling tests carry the same splice but assert a deny: `:195` (content push, splice at `:198`) and `:202` (compound, `:205`), plus the denied half of `:209` (`:215`). They pass on Windows only because the path fails to parse, not because of the shape they mean to check. They stay green but non-discriminating there.

`tests/helpers/shell-quote.js`'s `shellQuote` (from #4281) single-quotes a path for a Bash fixture while keeping every backslash, and `CQ_SINGLE` (`:323`, any run of non-quote characters between single quotes) admits it. This file already imports it (`:19`) and uses it at `:304`. A repo-wide sweep of `tests/hooks-*.test.js` for a double-quoted `"${…}"` path splice found no other site.

## Deliverables

1. Surface: infra

**Related:** #4149, #4210, #4211, #4242, #4244, #4245, #4247, #4248, #4294, #4303, #4309, #4310, #4328, #4329, #4304, #4369

Origin: /claude-tweaks:review of #4149 (refs #4149)

## Current State

In `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`, `scanHeredocsWith` (`:1554`) misreads two shapes and then strips the following lines as a data body:

- It treats a `<<` inside an unquoted `${…}` as a heredoc opener. Bash reads it as literal text.
- It treats a `$(cat <<EOF)` closed on the same line as an opener whose body is the following lines. Bash runs those lines.

The original executed probe ran at the #4149 branch and at 7070c0b8a: `echo ${x:-<<EOF}\n: > /M/zz\nEOF}` and `echo $(cat <<EOF)\n: > /M/zz\nEOF` both gave fileWriteTargets `[]`, and bash writes /M/zz. Found by /claude-tweaks:review of #4149 (lens 3b).

**Re-probed at HEAD (session cwd `/r`), still reproducing:** both probe commands give `fileWriteTargets` `[]`. The routine `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'` + newline + body + newline + `EOF` + newline + `)"` shape also gives `[]`, which is correct because its body is data.

The segment scanners already skip `${…}` via `spans.param` (`git-command.js:76`, `:1173`, `:1836`). The heredoc scanner does not apply the same span to find openers.

## Deliverables

1. Skip `<<` inside an unquoted `${…}` the way `spans.param` already does for the segment scanners.
2. Keep the body visible whenever a `$(` is still open at the opener and closes on the opener line, because the body then belongs to the substitution, not the next lines.
3. Add the probe cases to `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fileWriteTargets` reports /M/zz for both probe cases.
- The routine `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` shape still strips.
- Each new case goes red against the current scanner.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The worktree write guard no longer misses commands that follow text it wrongly took for the start of a heredoc.

## Technical Approach

Both fixes live in the opener scan. (1) Feed `spans.param` into `scanHeredocsWith`'s skip set so a `<<` inside `${…}` is never an opener candidate. (2) When an opener sits inside a `$(` whose matching `)` falls on the same line, a body cannot exist after that line, so do not start a body on the next line. Per bash, the here-document read for that substitution has no lines to consume before the `)`, so the following lines are ordinary commands. Judge both against real bash 3.2 and 5, per the repo-local `shell-scanner-bash-differential` skill, and time the adversarial shapes through `perf/heredoc-scan-linearity.test.js`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — `scanHeredocsWith` opener detection; reuse `spans.param`
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — the two probe cases plus the routine-shape guard
- `perf/heredoc-scan-linearity.test.js` — confirm the opener-scan change keeps the linear-time budget
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` — the heredoc parser-rules prose that names opener exceptions; update when the rules change

## Gotchas

- The fail-closed direction matters. When the scanner is unsure whether a `<<` opens a body, keeping the following lines visible (scanning them) is safe. Stripping them is what fails open. Prefer "not an opener" in ambiguous spans.
- `policy-schema-coverage.md` already documents that a heredoc opened inside a quoted `"$( … )"` is judged by that substitution's own command (#4210). Keep the new same-line-close rule consistent with that paragraph and pin it in prose there.
- #4309 (a backslash-newline-split command substitution in an unquoted heredoc body) and #4310 (a heredoc reader shadowed by a shell function) touch the same scanner. #4242 proposes splitting the lexer out, so expect conflicts.
- The perf linearity suite has an open over-budget case (#4329, the `"$( #"` write-scan case). Do not regress it further.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3942, #4038, #4163

Origin: #3950 final fix-wave re-review (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js`'s filing dedup survives a claim-heuristic change by matching each finding's `consolebackfill-{hash(itemId)}` item marker (#3950 fix wave, I1.5). One case still files a twin:

1. In one backfill pass, items A and B share a claim fingerprint. A is filed; B is planned as `reuse sameAs A`, so the created record carries only A's item marker.
2. The session crashes after the record is created and before `apply` settles B.
3. A plugin upgrade changes the claim cleaning before the next pass, so B's claim fingerprint moves.
4. The next pass finds A by its marker, but B matches neither its claim fingerprint nor its own marker, and is filed again.

Even when A's and B's new claims still match each other, the "matched an existing record" branch never records the fingerprint in the batch's filed map, so B does not fall back to `sameAs A` either. The digest path has the same shape: B's line was never posted, so B posts a second line under its new fingerprint.

Exposure is narrow — it needs a crash in that window, an upgrade between passes, and a same-claim pair — and the damage is one recoverable duplicate record or digest line.

## Deliverables

- A filing planned for item A also carries the item marker of every same-pass item planned `sameAs A`, so each of them is found by its own marker on the next pass.
- The "matched an existing record" branch records `fingerprint → record number` in the batch's filed map, so a later same-fingerprint item in the pass reuses it.
- The same treatment for digest lines: a digest duplicate planned `sameAs` a same-pass line is found by its own marker on the next pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test plans A and B with one claim fingerprint, simulates a crash after A's record is created, changes B's claim text, and re-plans: B reuses A's record and nothing is filed. The test fails against the code before the fix.
- A test where an existing record matches A and B shares A's fingerprint: B is `sameAs` that record, not a new filing.
- The digest equivalent of the first test: no second digest line for B.

## Release Note

Console backfill no longer files a duplicate record when a crash and a plugin upgrade both land between two passes over a same-claim pair.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js` — filing and digest planning
- `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill-dispose.test.js` — the three tests above

## Gotchas

- Premise probed at HEAD: the matched-record branch (`if (matched !== null)`, `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js:441-443`) pushes `reuse` without touching `batchFiled`, and only the new-filing branch calls `batchFiled.set(fp, d.itemId)` (`:447`). Confirmed.
- `batchFiled` maps a fingerprint to an **item id**, which a later `sameAs` resolves once that item's record exists. A matched existing record already has a number, so a later same-fingerprint item should reuse that number directly (`{ number: matched }`). Recording the number in the same map would need a value-shape distinction that its other readers do not expect.
- The item marker is `<!-- consolebackfill-item: {hash} -->` (`itemMarkerOf`, `:99-100`). Carrying several of them on one filed body must keep `filedRecordOf`'s marker lookup matching each marker independently.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #4197, #4164, #4162

Origin: second console-backfill pass after #3950 merged (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill.js` derives each finding's claim from the run's STAGED decision line. The #3950 fix wave made meta notes drop a clause at a time and treats `reason-not-auto:` and `same substance as … resolved Don't fix` as meta (`META_PAREN_RE`, `backfill.js:35`; the whole-clause patterns are `META_CLAUSE_RE`, `:32`). The second backfill pass over this repo still produced three bad claims out of 12 findings:

1. `share a location but not substance; both staged.` — the reproduction step's coordination note (`Reproduction: lens "3f" findings A / B share a location but not substance; both staged.`) became the whole claim of a finding at B. It was filed as #4196 and closed as not planned.
2. `(a future-dated heartbeatAt reads fresh; …). Lens 3a findings` — the next sentence's lead-in (`Lens 3a findings`) stays on the claim.
3. `(lastCommitMs duplicates the inline read; …) and` and `(stamp-site tests assert … would fail) and` — the joining `and` before the next finding stays on the claim.

Separately, item 2's stored location (`plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js:70`) was 25+ lines from the code it described at the current tip, so its judge could not cite evidence within 5 lines and it was filed as can't-tell (#4197) although the judge agreed with it in substance.

## Deliverables

- A note of the form `{findings} share a location but not substance; both staged` is meta: a claim made only of it is claim-empty, and the line yields no finding for it.
- A claim never ends in a dangling connective (`and`, `or`) or a following sentence's lead-in (`Lens 3x findings`, `Lens 3x finding`).
- Tests for each, taken from the three real lines above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `splitDecisionLine` (the exported entry point the existing tests use, `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill.test.js:165`), given a line ending `… plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md:63 / plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md:61 share a location but not substance; both staged.`, yields no finding whose claim is that note, for either location.
- The run-liveness line yields `a future-dated heartbeatAt reads fresh; fails safe toward live, makes a run unreapable until the clock passes it` with no trailing `Lens 3a findings`.
- The resume-freshness and stamp-site claims end without a trailing `and`.
- Each new test fails against the code before the fix.

## Release Note

Console backfill no longer files a reproduction step's coordination note as a finding, and finding claims no longer end in a stray connective.

## Technical Approach

Both defects are boundary problems in one cleaner. Add the coordination-note shape next to the existing whole-clause meta patterns (`META_CLAUSE_RE`, `backfill.js:32`). Add a trailing-fragment strip that mirrors the existing leading one (`LEAD_FRAGMENT_RE`, `:55`), so a segment never ends in `and`/`or` or a `Lens 3x finding(s)` lead-in. Drive every test through `splitDecisionLine` with the three real lines quoted above.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill.js` — claim cleaning: `META_CLAUSE_RE`/`META_PAREN_RE` (meta recognition), `splitPoints`/`analyseLine` (finding boundaries), `cleanSegment` (fragment strip)
- `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill.test.js` — the new cases

## Gotchas

- Premise correction: the filed Key Files named a `META_PHRASES` constant, but no such symbol exists in `backfill.js`. The meta patterns are `META_CLAUSE_RE` and `META_PAREN_RE`. The filed ACs called a `claim(…)` helper, but the module exports `splitDecisionLine`, not `claim`.
- A trailing-connective strip must stay boundary-anchored. A claim whose prose legitimately ends in a word like "reads and writes" keeps its words. Only a dangling connective left by the split is removed, the same "never a single word inside a kept claim" rule `META_CLAUSE_RE`'s comment states.
- Changing claim cleaning moves claim fingerprints for affected items. That interacts with #4162 (a same-claim pair filed across a crash and an upgrade).
- The stale-location half (item 2's `run-liveness/index.js:70` drifting 25+ lines) belongs to #4197, which is still open. It is not fixed here.

_Filed from the post-merge console-backfill pass._

## Original request

Console backfill keeps reproduction coordination notes and trailing connectives in finding claims

**Related:** #4197

Origin: second console-backfill pass after #3950 merged (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill.js` derives each finding's claim from the run's STAGED decision line. The #3950 fix wave made meta notes drop a clause at a time and treats `reason-not-auto:` and `same substance as … resolved Don't fix` as meta. The second backfill pass over this repo still produced three bad claims out of 12 findings:

1. `share a location but not substance; both staged.` — the reproduction step's coordination note (`Reproduction: lens "3f" findings A / B share a location but not substance; both staged.`) became the whole claim of a finding at B. It was filed as #4196 and closed as not planned.
2. `(a future-dated heartbeatAt reads fresh; …). Lens 3a findings` — the next sentence's lead-in (`Lens 3a findings`) stays on the claim.
3. `(lastCommitMs duplicates the inline read; …) and` and `(stamp-site tests assert … would fail) and` — the joining `and` before the next finding stays on the claim.

Separately, item 2's stored location (`plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js:70`) was 25+ lines from the code it described at the current tip, so its judge could not cite evidence within 5 lines and it was filed as can't-tell (#4197) although the judge agreed with it in substance.

## Deliverables

- A note of the form `{findings} share a location but not substance; both staged` is meta: a claim made only of it is claim-empty, and the line yields no finding for it.
- A claim never ends in a dangling connective (`and`, `or`) or a following sentence's lead-in (`Lens 3x findings`, `Lens 3x finding`).
- Tests for each, taken from the three real lines above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `claim('… plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md:63 / plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md:61 share a location but not substance; both staged.')` yields no claim for either location.
- The run-liveness line yields `a future-dated heartbeatAt reads fresh; fails safe toward live, makes a run unreapable until the clock passes it` with no trailing `Lens 3a findings`.
- The resume-freshness and stamp-site claims end without a trailing `and`.
- Each new test fails against the code before the fix.

## Release Note

Console backfill no longer files a reproduction step's coordination note as a finding, and finding claims no longer end in a stray connective.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill.js` — claim cleaning (META_PHRASES, split points, trailing-fragment strip)
- `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill.test.js` — the new cases

_Filed from the post-merge console-backfill pass._

Surface: infra

**Related:** #4149, #4281, #4244, #4246, #4294, #4211, #4242, #4247, #4248, #4303, #4309, #4310, #4328, #4329, #3822, #3982, #4217, #4292, #4304

Origin: /claude-tweaks:review of #4149 (refs #4149)

## Current State

**The defect is already fixed at HEAD.** #4281 (PR #4298, merged 2026-10-25, commit 1961010a1) taught `tokenize` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` to remove a backslash-newline, bare or double-quoted, the way bash does (`git-command.js:351-358`). It drops a word made only of backslash-newlines (`:437`). Re-probed at HEAD with session cwd `/r`:

- `cd /M && \` + newline + ` git commit -m x` gives `gitTargets` `[{action:'commit', dir:'/M'}]`.
- `git -C /M \` + newline + `  commit -m x` gives `[{action:'commit', dir:'/M'}]`.
- `true && \` + newline + ` cp x /M/b` gives `fileWriteTargets` `[{action:'copy', file:'/M/b'}]`.
- `cd /M && \` + newline + ` cp x b` gives `[{action:'copy', file:'/M/b'}]`.

When the record was filed (probe at the #4149 branch and 7070c0b8a), `tokenize` kept an unquoted backslash-newline as a stray `\` token that became `t[0]` of the next segment. So the command after `&& \` or `;\` was not seen as git or a write shape, and a `cd` after it was lost.

What is **not** yet pinned: `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js:776-780` ("#4281: a word of backslash-newlines alone is no word") covers `cd \` + newline + ` /main && git commit`, the continuation *inside* a `cd` argument. None of this record's own probes is a test case: a continuation after `&&`, a `git -C /M \` continuation before the subcommand, a `cp` after `&& \`, and the quoted-backslash-newline and heredoc-body preservation cases.

## Deliverables

1. Add this record's probe cases as regression tests: the two `gitTargets` cases and the two `fileWriteTargets` cases above, in `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` and `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js`.
2. Add the two preservation cases: a single-quoted backslash-newline (`echo 'a\` + newline + `b' > f` keeps the literal) and an unquoted-delimiter heredoc body line ending in `\`, which keeps its current, already-pinned joining behavior per `policy-schema-coverage.md`'s heredoc parser rules. Both are checked against real bash.
3. No production change unless a new case fails at HEAD. In that case it is a real residual defect, fixed here and named in the PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The four probe cases above pass at HEAD.
- Each of the four fails when `tokenize`'s backslash-newline removal (#4281) is reverted locally, which proves the tests discriminate.
- The single-quoted backslash-newline case keeps its literal, and the heredoc-body case's result is unchanged from HEAD.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Improved test coverage for the worktree write guard's handling of commands split across lines with a trailing backslash.

## Technical Approach

Tests only. Place the cases beside the existing #4281 block (`tests/hooks-git-command.test.js:698-800`), labelled `#4245`, so a reader sees which record each pin guards. Follow the repo-local `shell-scanner-bash-differential` skill's "judge each case against real bash 3.2 and 5" rule for the expected values.

### Key Files

- `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` — git-target and cd-walk continuation pins
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — write-target continuation pins
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — reference only, unless a new pin fails at HEAD

## Gotchas

- Premise drift: the filed Current State described HEAD-of-#4149 behavior. #4281 has since fixed the defect, so this record is now a regression pin. A reviewer who judges the existing #4281 test sufficient can close it as fixed by #4281 instead of building it.
- Prove each pin by reverting the #4281 continuation handling and watching it go red. A pin that passes either way guards nothing.
- #4244 and #4246 edit the same lexer, and #4242 proposes splitting it out. Tests added here move with whichever module the split creates.
- #4294 (open) covers line-continuation *redirect targets* on the span-mask tokenizer, an adjacent shape. Check that its fix and these pins agree on the same continuation semantics.

## Original request

Write gate misses the command after a backslash-newline line continuation

Origin: /claude-tweaks:review of #4149 (refs #4149)

## Current State

In `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`, `tokenize` keeps an unquoted backslash-newline as a stray `\` token, which becomes `t[0]` of the next segment, so the command after `&& \` or `;\` (or a `git -C /M \` continued onto the next line) is not seen as git or a write shape, and a `cd` after it is lost. Executed probe at the #4149 branch and at 7070c0b8a: `cd /M && \\\n git commit -m x` and `git -C /M \\\n  commit -m x` both give gitTargets `[]`. Multi-line `&& \` chains are common in agent-written commands. Found by /claude-tweaks:review of #4149 (lens 3b).

## Deliverables

1. Join an unquoted backslash-newline (outside single quotes and heredoc bodies) before segmenting, as bash does.
2. Add the probe cases to `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` and `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `gitTargets`/`fileWriteTargets` report the /M target for both probe cases and a `cp` after `&& \`.
- A quoted backslash-newline and a heredoc body line ending in `\` keep their current behavior.
- `npm test` passes.

_Filed by `review` via specShapedBody._
